Title: ABB COMLI
Question: How do I configure ABB COMLI in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
COMLI is an ABB Automation data transmission system used for communication between control systems and computers, utilizing serial, asynchronous data transmission in half duplex mode. This system operates based on a master/slave principle, where the master station initiates the message sequence, and the slave station responds. Implementation of COMLI in Adroit SCADA may differ when used alongside new data transmission systems like MMS.

Title: ABB COMLI
Topic: ABB COMLI 3
Question: How do I configure ABB COMLI 3 in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
ABB COMLI 3 connects Master and Slave systems via serial channels, requiring the same character format and transmission speed. The PLC programs on each system control the communication by activating memory cells to transmit messages, and the Slave responds with information or an acknowledgement.

Title: About Adroit Database Files (Agent Storage)
Question: What is About Adroit Database Files (Agent Storage)?
Answer:
The Adroit database file (.WGP) is a central component of the Agent Server, storing data and configuration for all agents within a project. This file includes information for agents that are manually created and dynamic agents such as Proxy and Scan agents, excluding those automatically generated. It's crucial to regularly back up this file to prevent data loss, and it's loaded after all agent type (.DLL) files have been loaded by the Agent Server.

Title: About Adroit Projects
Question: What is About Adroit Projects?
Answer:
Adroit Projects allow multiple distributed Agent Servers to share agents and data seamlessly. If Agent Servers share the same project name and are on the same network domain, they can refer to each other's agents. Project names should be unique across standalone and distributed Agent Servers, and are configured in the Agent Server Configuration page.

Title: About Adroit Projects
Question: What is About Adroit Projects?
Answer:
A project in Adroit , is the default mechanism for allowing multiple distributed Agent Servers to seamlessly share their agents and the data that they contain. In other words, if Agent Server A and Agent Server B have the SAME project name (and are in the same network domain), then Agent Server A is able to refer to agents within Agent Server B and vice verse.

Title: About Agent Data (Slots)
Question: What is About Agent Data (Slots)?
Answer:
Agent data, referred to as agent attributes or slots, are externally accessible data points associated with each agent instance. These slots are defined as attributes of the agent and can be accessed by the Agent Server. Slots contain data of various types, such as ASCII strings, floating-point numbers, or Boolean values, depending on the agent type.

Alarm acknowledgement in Adroit refers to the process of acknowledging alarms or incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, indicating an operator has understood and responded to an event requiring attention. Title: About DataBinders
Topic: The main difference between a Select query and a DataBinder
Question: What is the main difference between a Select query and a DataBinder?
Answer:
A Select query returns a static snapshot of data at the time of the query, while a DataBinder continuously communicates with the database, allowing for a ‘live’ view and modification of data within the database, including adding or removing records. To use a DataBinder, you create a graphic form and add the VIZNETDataBinder component, configuring it to display data from specified tables and fields.

Title: About Power Factor
Question: What is About Power Factor?
Answer:
Power factor is the ratio of real power (watts) to apparent power (volt-amperes) in an alternating current (A.C.) electrical system. A power factor below 1.0 means the electricity provider must generate more current than necessary, leading to increased costs that may be passed on to customers. Maintaining a power factor greater than 0.85 helps to optimize energy usage and minimize costs.
Category: Smart UI - About
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: power factor, wattage, volt-amperes, reactive power

Title: About Power Factor
Question: What is About Power Factor?
Answer:
Power factor is a measure of how efficiently electrical power is being used. Reactive power, generated by inductive loads like transformers and motors, can cause the apparent power to exceed the real power component, negatively impacting the power factor. Power factor correction involves adjusting the balance between inductive and capacitive loads to bring the power factor closer to unity.

Document Type: help
Section Type: help

Title: About SNMP Traps

Answer:
SNMP traps are unsolicited SNMP messages sent by devices to an SNMP manager to notify them of significant events. These traps can be simple or complex, containing one or more OIDs. To enable trap receipt, check the 'Enable traps' checkbox in the Connection settings of the Edit SNMP Manager Agent dialog, and ensure polling is also enabled.

Title: About SNMP Traps
Question: What is About SNMP Traps?
Answer:
The SNMP Traps indicator helps you determine which tag to use for storing trap values. When the SNMPManager agent receives traps, it stores them in a queue and, when triggered, transfers the trap variable to designated slots for use by a script. It is important to enable polling to receive traps and note that once a trap is read from the queue, it is discarded.
Category: Smart UI - About
Document Type: help

Title: About SNMP Traps
Question: What is About SNMP Traps?
Answer:
SNMP traps are unsolicited SNMP messages sent by devices to an SNMP manager to notify them of significant events. These traps can be simple (one OID) or complex (multiple OIDs) and are used to reduce the amount of data that needs to be monitored by polling. To enable SNMP traps for an SNMPMgr agent, you must check the 'Enable traps' checkbox in the Connection settings of the Edit SNMPMgr Agent dialog and enable polling.

Title: About SNMP Traps
Question: What is About SNMP Traps?
Answer:
SNMP traps are incoming messages received by the Adroit agent for monitoring device events. The agent stores these traps in a queue and transfers them to slots for use by domain-specific scripts when trapPop is set to 1. Enabling polling is required to receive traps, and the SNMP Trap Service must be installed alongside the SNMP Service.

Title: About the GSM_SMS driver

The GSM_SMS driver sends and receives SMS messages to and from SMS GSM modems. Title: Accumulator Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Slot List for the Agent
Question: What is Slot List for the Agent?
Answer:
The Agent utilizes various slot types, distinguished by color: red slots are configuration slots, blue slots are operator/process driven, and other slots are agent-controlled. The Agent maintains a history of differential values using the VARSTRING slot, which can be configured with a connection string to a SQL Server database via the Adroit Config Editor. The deadband slot desensitizes value alarm limits, while the disableOnStandby boolean prevents duplicate SQL queries on standby servers. The elapsedTime slot captures the time elapsed in minutes, and the inputTag defines the accumulating process value.
Category: Smart UI - Agents
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: agent, slots, configuration, database, deadband

Title: Accumulator Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Slot List for the Agent
Question: What is Slot List for the Agent?
Answer:
The Agent uses the inputValue slot to store the ever-increasing process value. The interval slot defines the duration of each period, and intervalMode determines how the interval is specified, using the intervalTag or system time. This allows the agent to calculate differential increases in value over a defined period.

Title: Accumulator Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Specifications
Question: What is Specifications?
Answer:
The Accumulator Agent utilizes status bits to indicate alarm conditions. Specifically, status bit 17 indicates a SQL error, status bit 18 indicates a VHighHigh alarm, status bit 19 indicates a VHigh alarm, status bit 20 indicates a VLow alarm, status bit 21 indicates a VLowLow alarm, status bit 22 indicates an RHighHigh alarm, status bit 23 indicates an RHigh alarm, status bit 24 indicates an RLow alarm, and status bit 25 indicates an RLowLow alarm. These bits are pulsed on and off based on differential value comparisons.

Title: Accumulator Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Slot List for the Agent
Question: What is Slot List for the Agent?
Answer:
The 'Slot List' for the agent is a collection of rate alarm limits used to trigger alerts based on changes in the differential value. Specifically, this includes rateHiHi, rateHi, rateLo, and rateLoLo, which are used with different alarm types (RHighHigh, RHigh, RLow, RLowLow) when the rate reaches or exceeds the defined limit. This slot is only applicable when using intervalMode of 0, 1, or 2.

Answer:
The Slot List for the Agent allows you to define multiple alarm limits for various value types, including high, high-high, and low. Title: ACK Commands
Question: What is ACK Commands?
Answer:
ACK Commands are used to acknowledge alarms reported by an agent within the Agent Server. This command must be enabled by the Command agent to which it is sent, and can be performed via SMS or Putslot. You can acknowledge a specific alarm for a specified agent, or all alarms relating to an agent.

Title: AcknowledgeAtStartup
Question: What is AcknowledgeAtStartup?
Answer:
AcknowledgeAtStartup automatically acknowledges alarms when the Agent Server starts. To enable this, set the registry value HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\[Wow6432Node]SOFTWARE\[Adroit Technologies]\[Adroit]\[Workgroup]\[WG.INI (REG_)DWORD to 1. Do not set this value to 0, as it will result in unacknowledged alarms.

Title: AcknowledgeAtStartup
Question: What is AcknowledgeAtStartup?
Answer:
AcknowledgeAtStartup is a registry setting that forces the Agent Server to automatically acknowledge alarms at startup. To enable this, set the value of HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\[software]\[adroit technologies]\[adroit]\[workgroup]\[wg.ini] (REG_DWORD) to 1. However, we do not recommend setting this value to 0, as it will result in unacknowledged alarms.

Title: Active Clusters Foundation
Topic: Clustering Agent Servers
Question: What is Clustering Agent Servers?
Answer:
Clustered Agent Servers, previously known as hot standby, provide client and server redundancy for high availability of the system. These servers replicate a database (WGP file) on the same project, with one server acting as the master and the other as a standby. If the master server fails, the standby server takes over, ensuring continued operation of the UI and scanning tasks.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: clustering, redundancy, agent server, standby server

Title: Active Clusters Foundation
Topic: Clustering Agent Servers
Question: What is Clustering Agent Servers?
Answer:
Clustered Agent Servers, also known as hot standby, provide redundancy for clients and servers, enabling high availability of the system. These servers replicate a database (WGP file) on the same project and can be networked with other Agent Servers. If the master server fails, the standby server takes over, and the UI and scanning tasks continue to operate.

Title: Adding allowed users and groups

Topic: General Overview
Question: What is General Overview?

Adroit is a product designed to connect with various third-party devices such as PLCs, OPC servers, and RTUs. It utilizes a protocol driver to communicate with these devices, supporting over 100 different protocols. The system is comprised of a Front End Device (FED), Agent Server (AS), and SmartUI Server (SUIS) working together to provide real-time data access and visualization.

Title: Adroit Installation Read Me

Question: What is Adroit Installation Read Me?
Answer:
When loading a Agent Database (.wgp) file from a previous version of Adroit, Adroit 10 uses the saved status bit information to configure the IO flags setting of all the Device agents and when the Agent Database (.wgp) file is saved then these status bits are switched OFF in the Agent Database (.wgp) file. IMPORTANT: When starting the Adroit 10 Agent Server for the first time and loading a Agent Database (.wgp) file from a previous version, devices will most likely NEVER show healthy once all the devices are started.

Title: Adroit Logging Factor
Question: What is Adroit Logging Factor?
Answer:
Adroit Logging Factor was originally designed in 1992 to limit log file size to 20% of expected data volume due to limitations in CPU, HDD speeds, and serial protocol speeds. This compression factor was removed for new installations, but legacy WGP files can still cause issues if logging periods exceed 5,000,000 samples (95 MB) per Datalog agent. To resolve this, you can reset the LogCompressionFactor value to 5 or reduce the logging periods of affected agents by a factor of 5.
Category: Smart UI - Logging
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: logging, Adroit, compression, Datalog agents
Source URL: https://ats-adroit.github.io/mysoftware-help/chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/AU_01_08/Adroit_Logging_Factor.htm
Source File: chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/AU_01_08/Adroit_Logging_Factor.htm

Title: Adroit Logging Factor
Question: What is Adroit Logging Factor?
Answer:
Adroit Logging Factor was originally designed in 1992 to compress log data, aiming for a 20% log file size based on the limitations of CPU, HDD speeds, and serial protocol speeds. However, this compression factor has been removed for new installations to avoid misleading users, and legacy WGP files can cause issues if logging periods exceed 95 MB per Datalog agent. To resolve this, you can either set the LogCompressionFactor registry value to 5 or reconfigure the logging periods of affected Datalog agents, typically dividing the current logging period by 5.
Category: Classic UI - Logging
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: Adroit Logging Factor, logging, compression, Datalog agents

Title: Adroit Tag to Database Field Mapping
Topic: Tag to Database Field Mapping
Question: What is Tag to Database Field Mapping?
Answer:
Tag to Database Field Mapping in Adroit establishes a connection between specific tag values (like `agentName.slotName`) and the corresponding database field. This mapping is required for each transaction type, ensuring that data from Adroit is correctly written to the designated database table. Each mapping includes an Index, Tag, Field, and optionally a Field format to control how data is formatted before transmission.
Category: Smart UI - Configuration
Document Type: configuration
Section Type: configuration
Keywords: tag, database, mapping, field

Title: Adroit Tag to Database Field Mapping
Topic: Tag to Database Field Mapping
Question: What is Tag to Database Field Mapping?
Answer:
Tag to Database Field Mapping establishes a link between Adroit tags (like `agentName.slotName`) and specific database fields. Each mapping defines how data from an Adroit transaction is sent to a corresponding field within the connected database table, with the exception of delete transactions. This process involves mapping tag values to field names, optionally formatting data before sending it to the database.

Title: Adroit_Project_Path environmental variable
Question: What is the Adroit_Project_Path environmental variable?
Answer:
The ‘adroit_project_path’ environment variable is created automatically by Adroit when applications like PSEXE.exe, Adroit .exe, and others are started. This variable specifies the path to the currently active configuration within the Program Data folder, typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default. It ensures the application always points to the correct configuration.

Title: AdroitCOM API Reference 10.0.5.1
Question: What are the specifications for AdroitCOM API Reference 10.0.5.1?
Answer:
The AdroitCOM API Reference 10.0.5.1 includes three assemblies: AdroitCOM.dll, Interop.AdroitCOMLib.dll, and as_api.dll. AdroitCOM.dll is the COM wrapper for as_api, Interop.AdroitCOMLib.dll facilitates access via a managed (.NET) application, and as_api.dll provides access to the Agent Server via unmanaged applications.

Document Type: spec_sheet

Title: AdroitCOM API Reference 10.0.5.1
Topic: AdroitCOM API Reference 10.0.5.1 2
Question: What are the specifications for AdroitCOM API Reference 10.0.5.1?
Answer:
The AdroitCOM API Reference 10.0.5.1 includes the i.dll assembly, which provides access to the Agent Server for unmanaged applications. Key methods include GetApiPath, GetServerList, GetVersion, and SetTimeout, used for establishing paths, retrieving server lists, determining the version, and setting timeouts. Scanning functionalities are available through ScanTag and ScanTagEx, which scan tags based on specified parameters.

Title: Advanced Scanning Settings
Question: What is Advanced Scanning Settings?
Answer:
The Advanced Scanning Settings allow you to configure global scanning settings that affect scanning, including demand scanning, agent server startup behavior, tag tagging, and text agent conversions. These settings primarily manage the New Adroit Scanning Architecture (NASA) protocol driver, allowing you to optimize scan tasks and handle tag status updates in real-time. Turning on certain features, like allowing changes to scan-inhibit and output-enable to affect tags immediately, can increase server subscriptions and slightly impact device stopping and starting times.

Title: Advanced Scanning Settings
Question: What is Advanced Scanning Settings?
Answer:
Advanced Scanning Settings reverse the rawValue slot and place this value into the value slot of the agent. By default, this is cleared. This setting impacts all Multistate agents and allows you to resend the Adroit value to the front-end device when a tag receives a value different from the current Adroit value, provided the tag’s scan inhibit bit is on. Checking 'Check for Comm port availability' enables the device configuration dialog to verify port availability, but should be disabled when connecting to virtual ports like MOXA.
Category: Smart UI - Configuration
Document Type: configuration
Section Type: configuration
Keywords: scanning, agent, adroit, ports
Source URL: https://ats-adroit.github.io/mysoftware-help/chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/AU_01_02/Advanced_Scanning_Settings.htm

Answer:
Agent Bad signifies that an agent has encountered an internal error, such as an Analog value being out of range, incorrect expression syntax, or an invalid state in a MultiState. When Agent Bad is set, the BAD bit (00) is also set, indicating a critical issue.

Title: Agent List CSV File Format
Question: What is Agent List CSV File Format?
Answer:
The Agent List CSV file is created when an Alarm agent is exported and stores the alarmed agents. The file follows the format xxxxx-AGNTLST.CSV, with columns including Tagname, Typeindex, Route number, Acknowledge, Inhibit time, Delay time, and Conditional expression. The Typeindex is calculated based on the TYPLST.CSV file.

Title: Agent List CSV File Format
Question: What is Agent List CSV File Format?
Answer:
The Agent List CSV file is created when an Alarm agent is exported and stores the alarmed agents. Title: Agent Naming Convention
Question: What is Agent Naming Convention?
Answer:
Agent names must be 32 characters or less and cannot be the same as Agent Types or Agent Groups. Agent names also cannot contain spaces, percent signs, commas, periods, backslashes, or dollar signs.

Title: Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling)
Question: What is Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling)?
Answer:
Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring uses the statusBad bit within the agent or slot status word to determine if an agent or slot is experiencing problems. This statusBad bit combines statusConnectionBad, statusScanBad, and statusAgentBad, indicating potential issues with connectivity, scanning, or the agent itself. The statusScanBad bit is automatically set during startup if the slot has been scanned, resetting upon a successful scan transaction.

are files that store the data calculated by a Counter or Statistical agent. Their purpose is to ensure that none of this data is lost. However, this practice is dangerous as .WGP files can corrupt if a power failure occurs during the save.

Title: Agent Server Communication within Networks
Question: What is Agent Server Communication within Networks?
Answer:
Agent Servers connected with the same project name communicate through broadcasts, allowing direct access to other servers within that project. This approach is effective for small networks on the same domain but becomes inflexible for larger, inter-domain, or WAN-connected networks, or networks with limited bandwidth like 10MB WLANs. Explicit Agent Server connections are required for these configurations.

Document Type: help

Title: Agent Server Communication within Networks
Question: What is Agent Server Communication within Networks?
Answer:
Agent Servers with the same project name connect via broadcasts to allow direct access to other servers within the project. This approach is suitable for small, same-domain networks but inflexible for inter-domain or large networks. Agent Server broadcasts do not operate across domains or WANs, and maintaining a large, fully connected grid can be resource-intensive.

Title: Agent Server Connection Methods
Question: What is Agent Server Connection Methods?
Answer:
Adroit provides two methods for connecting Agent Servers: Project Name and Explicit Agent Server Connections. The Project Name method allows Agent Servers within the same project to seamlessly share agents and data through network broadcasts, but it's limited by network infrastructure and doesn't always result in efficient communication. Explicit Agent Server Connections allow you to connect Agent Servers on different networks, but require manual configuration and can create unnecessary network traffic.
Category: Smart UI - Agents

Title: Agent Server Connection Methods
Question: What is Agent Server Connection Methods?
Answer:
Agent Server connection methods allow two-way access to agents by adding the Agent Server’s project or server name to the remote Agent Server’s Projects / Servers list. This mechanism requires enabling the Additional connections checkbox in the Project Options dialog for both Agent Servers. It utilizes Agent Server broadcasts, but these do not function across domains or routers, necessitating an explicit connection for servers on different networks. Configuration is performed using the Adroit Config Editor by specifying the Project Name and Agent Server Name, and ensuring the Additional connections checkbox is checked on both servers.

Title: Agent Server Master Write Scanning Strategy
Topic: Operation of strategy:
Question: What is Operation of strategy?
Answer:
The Agent Server monitors scanned tags from front-end devices (PLCs) and writes their values back to the devices. When the Agent Server starts, it initializes the tag values to the last saved WGP value if SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan is set to 1. The server also writes values back when devices start or stop, or after a communication failure is resolved.

Document Type: help

Title: Agent Server Master Write Scanning Strategy
Topic: Operation of strategy:
Question: What is Operation of strategy?
Answer:
The Agent Server Master Write Scanning Strategy synchronizes process values from front-end devices (PLCs) to the Agent Server. Initially, when the Agent Server starts, it sets process values to the last saved WGP value if SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan is enabled. Subsequently, the Agent Server writes updated tag values to the PLCs when a device changes state or communications are restored after a failure.

Title: Agent Subscriptions
Question: What is Agent Subscriptions?
Answer:
Agent Subscriptions are a mechanism for receiving updates asynchronously from an Agent tag. This allows changes to be sent to registered listeners without requiring explicit data reads, resulting in a more responsive and efficient communication system between the Agent Server and connected clients like Operators.

Title: Agent Type Slot Reference
Question: What is Agent Type Slot Reference?
Answer:
Agent Type Slots are named values (attributes) within an agent that can be retrieved and/or set by the Agent Server. These slots are categorized, including common slots like Header Slots and type-specific slots like Accumulator Agent Slots, which accumulate values over time. Agents utilize slots to manage data, such as alarms, coordinates, or process values, and these slots can be referenced using fully qualified names like `agentName.slotName`.

Answer:
The Agent Used By Inquiry feature identifies other agents that have directly joined a specific agent. This includes agents like Expression, Scan, and Datalog, but not Script agents that utilize the agent within their scripts, or agents not explicitly joined. This is crucial for removing agents, ensuring all references are deleted before removal.

Title: Alarm Agent - Database File Format
Question: What is Alarm Agent - Database File Format?
Answer:
The Alarm Agent database file format uses a series of lists to define alarms and routing. These lists include information on alarm types, routing times, and the agents associated with each alarm. The file is structured with elements like DPER, PRTY, and TYPLST, representing data persistence, priority, and alarm type lists respectively.

Title: Alarm Agent - Database File Format
Question: What is Alarm Agent - Database File Format?
Answer:
The Alarm Agent database file format stores alarm event data using lists of types, routes, and agents. These lists include details like alarm priorities, routing time deadbands, and agent-specific information such as alarm types and routes. The file format consists of several key indicator lists, including TYPLST (alarm types), ROUTLST (alarm routes), and AGNTLST (alarmed agents), each with associated data values.

Title: Alternate Secondary Port Enabled
Question: What is Alternate Secondary Port Enabled?
Answer:
Alternate Secondary Port Enabled allows Adroit to use a different PLC address if a primary communication channel fails, particularly for network-able communications like RS485, RS232, Ethernet, and Modbus. This feature is activated when a Read or Write transaction times out and retries fail, causing the driver to attempt communication through an alternate port (address Y). Once communication is established through the secondary port, the driver will revert back to the primary port if the secondary port fails.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help

Title: Alternate Secondary Port Enabled
Question: What is Alternate Secondary Port Enabled?
Answer:
Alternate Secondary Port Enabled allows Adroit to use different PLC addresses to avoid communication failures with hardware components. If a Read or Write transaction fails, the Adroit driver will attempt communication through a secondary PLC address, which is configured when a timeout occurs during the initial attempt. Communications will then switch back to the primary port if the secondary port also fails, allowing scanning to resume.
Category: Classic UI - Other
Document Type: help

Title: AnalogRawComms
Question: What is AnalogRawComms?
Answer:
AnalogRawComms allows you to communicate alarm limits and provide reverse polarity for Analog agents. Specifically, setting the registry value `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\[Wow6432Node]SOFTWARE\[Adroit Technologies]\[Adroit]` to 1 disables automatic validity checking of alarm values and ensures the Engmax value is lower than the Engmin value.

Title: ARec Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Specifications
Question: What is Specifications?
Answer:
The ARecStatus bits, specifically bits 16 through 31 (ARecStatus00 to ARecStatus15), are boolean values controlled through configuration and sequence operations. These status bits are managed by the state and sequence operations and should not be driven by both unless different status bits are being used.

Title: Assigning values to aliases
Topic: To manually assign values to aliases defined in the hosted graphic form:
Question: What is To manually assign values to aliases defined in the hosted graphic form?
Answer:
To manually assign values to aliases in the hosted graphic form, first select the TemplateGO control and expose the data element to be assigned to the first alias within the Enterprise Manager. If the property does not appear, customize the control to display the Edit Common Properties dialog and highlight the required property before clicking Finish. Finally, use the Select Item To Connect To dialog to choose the alias and click Finish, repeating these steps for each alias until all are assigned.

Question: What is Audit Agent - Database File Format?
Answer:
The Audit Agent - Database File Format defines the structure of files used to record audit data. This format includes lines specifying agent names and an end-of-list indicator. The file uses the ENA flag to indicate whether a line is enabled, and LST fields contain agent names.

Title: Audit Agent - Database File Format
Question: What is Audit Agent - Database File Format?
Answer:
The Audit Agent - Database File Format defines a file that lists the agents being audited. The file contains a list of agent names, where each agent is identified by 'agent name' and followed by an end-of-list indicator. The 'ENA' parameter indicates whether the audit is enabled (1) or disabled (0).

Title: Audit Policy
Question: What is Audit Policy?
Answer:
Audit Policy in Windows tracks selected user activities by logging security events, recording both successful and unsuccessful attempts to perform actions. These events are placed in the computer’s security log, which can be reviewed using Event Viewer. The policy affects domain controllers and servers in the domain, or just the local computer if it's not a domain controller.

Title: Authorizing changes made to values
Question: What is Authorizing changes made to values?
Answer:
Authorizing changes made to values is required when data elements have been configured to require authorization via the Smart UI Designer. This process involves using the Authorize Data Element Writes dialog to grant write access to a value (data element) when the currently logged-on user does not have sufficient permissions, providing a username and password of a user with write access, and optionally, including comments to justify the change. If the user already has write access, the dialog is still displayed to authorize the changes.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: authorization, data elements, Smart UI Designer
Source URL: https://ats-adroit.github.io/mysoftware-help/chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Operator/10Cfg/40Mng/10Sec/Authorizing_changes_made_to_values.htm

---

Title: Authorizing deferred writes to data elements
Question: What is Authorizing deferred writes to data elements?
Answer:
Authorizing deferred writes to data elements is a process used when a data element’s security settings require authorization, but this authorization cannot be performed immediately through the Authorize Data Element Writes dialog. Instead, you click the Defer button to add the write to a list of deferred changes. This list is dynamically maintained, reflecting the most recent change, and is automatically removed when a newer change is made. To authorize these changes, you must be a permitted Smart UI Server user with write access, and you cannot be the user who originally made the change.
Category: Smart UI - Other

Title: AutoConnect ActiveX Property
Question: What is AutoConnect ActiveX Property?
Answer:
The AutoConnect ActiveX property is a boolean setting that instructs an object to automatically connect to a server or track a master node. When set to TRUE, the object will connect to the server defined in the Server property or the master node in the Cluster property, automatically tracking the master node in cluster operation. The ConnectionUpdate callback method is invoked before switching to a new master node.

Title: Automatic master mode assignment
Topic: Rules and implications
Question: What is Rules and implications?
Answer:
New cluster servers can automatically become masters after a configurable period of time after startup, provided they haven't detected another cluster server. If no other servers are detected, the server becomes master based on alphabetical name. Adding or removing a server doesn't automatically change master status; however, changing a server's serverMode or serverState slots can trigger master mode transitions.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: master, cluster, server, mode

Title: Automatic master mode assignment
Topic: An automatic election for master mode at a healthy standby server will occur when:
Question: What is An automatic election for master mode at a healthy standby server will occur when?
Answer:
An automatic election for master mode occurs when a healthy master server becomes unhealthy or when the user sets a standby server to master mode. The Adroit system then ensures that the old master is relegated to standby, preventing multiple master servers from existing in the cluster.

Topic: Suggested method of operation
Question: What is Suggested method of operation?
Answer:
The server with the lowest alphabetical name will automatically become the master server when both Agent Servers are started. If a master server fails, the standby server will take over, and the UI will automatically switch to the new master.

Title: Automatic master mode assignment
Topic: Rules and implications
Question: What is Rules and implications?
Answer:
New cluster servers can automatically become master after a configured period following startup, provided no other master exists in the cluster. If multiple servers are present, the server alphabetically closest to 'a' will elect itself as master. Adding a new server doesn't automatically change master status, but removing the master server will cause the next alphabetically closest standby server to become master.

Title: Automatic WGP File Backups
Question: What is Automatic WGP File Backups?
Answer:
Automatic WGP file backups are created each time an Adroit WGP file is saved, ensuring that only the changes made since the last save are preserved. These backups are named with a date, time, and version number, and are located in the same folder as the WGP file. Restoring these files requires manually stopping the Agent Server and renaming files.

Title: Automatic WGP File Backups
Question: What is Automatic WGP File Backups?
Answer:
Automatic WGP file backups create a copy of your WGP file each time it's saved. These backups preserve changes since the last save and are stored in the same folder as the original WGP file, following a specific naming convention based on the date and time of the save. Restoring a WGP file requires stopping the Agent Server, renaming the file, and then renaming the backup file to that name and restarting the Agent Server.

Title: Backing Up Adroit Database (.WGP) Files
Question: What is Backing Up Adroit Database (.WGP) Files?
Answer:
Steps: The Adroit database or .WGP file stores almost all of the data and configuration of the Agent Server, including the added agents, their values and their alarming, logging and scanning configuration. For this reason, it is essential that this file, along with the other Adroit project files, be frequently backed up to ensure that the integrity of this data is preserved. Since if this file is either deleted or becomes corrupted without having a recent backup, many man hours of effort will be lost.

Title: BACnet Ethernet UDP-IP
Topic: 1. Overview
Question: How do I configure 1. Overview in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
This driver utilizes the BACnet Stack library and supports functions like ReadProperty and ReadPropertyMultiple. When ReadPropertyMultiple fails, the driver reverts to ReadProperty, which has a limitation of 255 items. Ensure broadcasting is enabled on routers and internal networks, and that UDP is enabled through firewalls, using UDP port 47808.
Category: Drivers
Document Type: driver

Title: Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents
Question: What is Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents?
Answer:
DbAccess Agents manage transactions within databases by establishing a connection to a database and identifying the relevant table. These agents support various transactions like insert, update, delete, and retrieve, allowing data transfer between Adroit and the database. Agents can be triggered on demand, scheduled, or by tag changes, with scheduling offering options like every three seconds or every twenty-four hours.
Category: Smart UI - Agents
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: DbAccess Agent, transactions, database, Adroit

---

Title: Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents
Question: What is Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents?
Answer:
Each DbAccess Agent represents a transaction on a row, in a table, in a database. Before any transactions can take place, a connection to a database has to be established and a table in this database has to be identified, that requires or contains the information necessary for a transaction. IMPORTANT: If you are connecting to a database across the network and your Agent Server is running as a service, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the remote database.

Title: Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit
Question: What is Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit?
Answer:
Adroit cluster servers can be assigned to different modes – master, standby, or normal – using the systeminfo.serverMode (0, 1, 2) and systeminfo.serverState (0, 1) slots. A new server always starts as standby, and the serverstate is initially set to healthy. Users can manually change the serverstate to unhealthy (0) to relinquish the master state if they detect an issue.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help

Answer:
Adroit cluster servers can be configured in three modes: master, standby, or normal. A new server always begins as standby, and the serverstate slot is initially set to healthy. Users can manually or automatically change a server's state to unhealthy, triggering a transition to standby.

Title: Best Practices
Topic: Project Directory Structure
Question: What is Project Directory Structure?
Answer:
The Adroit Software should be separated from configured project(s) to facilitate backups and upgrades. A project folder should be created at the root drive (e.g., 'C:\_Data\_Adroit\_Configurations\_Default') and contain directories for CSV data, custom agents, Agent Server configurations, datalogs, mimics, wizards, and work files. The \_Mimics subfolder is automatically added to the Adroit Path.

Document Type: help

Bulk Scanning or Scanning Import allows you to configure scanning for a large number of tags on a device by exporting scanning configurations to a spreadsheet, modifying it, and then importing it back into Adroit. This method is recommended when adding more than 100 scan points to the same device. Before importing, ensure communications are working, back up your database, and scan at least one tag to verify the configuration.

Title: Calculating statistics from Analog values
Question: What is Calculating statistics from Analog values?
Answer:
The Analog agent can calculate statistics like sum, average, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, and direction of change from its value slot. These statistics are calculated over a rolling period (statsPeriod) specified in minutes, recording the value every second within that timeframe. The calculated statistics are stored in slots named statsAverage, statsMax, statsMin, statsStdDev, statsSum, and statsDirection, which can be reported as needed.
Category: Smart UI - Logging
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: statistics, Analog agent, statsPeriod, trend

Title: Calculating statistics from Analog values
Question: What is Calculating statistics from Analog values?
Answer:
Calculating statistics from Analog values involves setting the statsDirDev slot to a decimal percentage (between 0 and 1). Deviations in value less than or equal to this percentage will result in the statsDirection slot being set to 0, indicating 'no change'.

Title: Calculations in Expressions
Topic: Examples of expressions . An expression can be thought of as a collection of terms associated by mathematical operators, which are evaluated in a strict order of precedence. Mathematical Operators . Mathematical Functions . This order can be overridden by using brackets. Each term of the expression is composed of primary elements, which can either be signed (or complemented) numbers or variables (v1 to v20, and v99 which is equivalent to "value"), or sub-expressions. This recursive definition of an expression means that expressions can be nested to any level of complexity. Note
Question: What is an expression?
Answer:
An expression is a collection of terms associated by mathematical operators, evaluated in a strict order of precedence. Expressions can be nested to any level of complexity and include numbers, variables (v1-v20 and v99), or sub-expressions, and can be documented with C-style comments.

Title: Catch-up
Question: What is Catch-up?
Answer:
Catch-up is a method used to synchronize historical data on a new server added to a cluster. Specifically, the SystemDatalog agent facilitates this process by catching up the data between two specified date/times, ensuring the server mirrors the active member of the cluster.

Graphic elements with enclosed areas, such as Ellipse, Rectangle, Polyline, Spline, Text, and Scale, can be colored and filled. The Command agent utilizes 'slots' to manage SMS message delivery. Specifically, the `GSM_SMS device slot` is used to connect to the GSM_SMS device and send/receive messages. Title: Common Reasons for Scanning Import Failure
Question: What is Common Reasons for Scanning Import Failure?
Answer:
Scanning import failures can occur due to several reasons, including a missing tag, an unrecognized scan address, a slot already scanned, or a timeout. To resolve these issues, ensure the tag exists, try a different scan address, check the slot status, or increase the Advanced Agent sever remote timeout value. Generating an alarm on route 0 will allow you to view alarm details.

Title: Common Status Bits of the Multistate Agent
Question: What is Common Status Bits of the Multistate Agent?
Answer:
If the MultiState agent enters an undefined state, it will report as being in State00 and set the AGENT BAD bit, and the BAD bit will also be set. This behavior occurs only during a transition from a valid state to an invalid state, and a new, unconfigured agent will not have its BAD bits set.

Title: Communication Hardware and Cluster Server I/O Modes
Question: What is Communication Hardware and Cluster Server I/O Modes?
Answer:
Communication Hardware Cluster Server I/O modes define how devices connect and communicate. These modes include parallel scanning, shadowing, and network configurations, each with specific use cases. Parallel and shadowing modes are point-to-point, typically using RS232C, while network modes allow multiple masters to participate simultaneously, such as with L2 bus or Ethernet networks.

Title: Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user)
Question: What is Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user)?
Answer:
Condition Bits function as a 'fan-in' mechanism, meaning an agent condition bit automatically becomes 1 when one of its corresponding slot condition bits is 1. However, setting an agent condition bit does not automatically set the slot bits. The agent status retains a raw and derived status word to maintain the original setting.
Category: Smart UI - Security
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: condition bits, agent, slot

Title: Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user)
Question: What is Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user)?
Answer:
Condition Bits utilize a fan-in mechanism where an agent condition bit automatically becomes 1 if any of its corresponding slot condition bits are 1. However, setting an agent condition bit does not automatically set the slot condition bits. The agent status retains a raw and a derived status word, ensuring user or system-set agent bits are preserved.

Title: Configuring Accumulator Agents
Topic: IntervalMode options 0 - 2
Question: What is IntervalMode options 0 - 2?
Answer:
IntervalMode options 0-2 define how the end of an interval is triggered based on changes to the intervalTag. Option 0 sets the interval tag value to zero, triggering the interval end. Option 1 sets the interval tag value from zero to non-zero, and Option 2 triggers when the intervalTag value changes to any other value.

Title: Configuring Accumulator Agents
Topic: IntervalMode options 3 - 4
Question: What is IntervalMode options 3 - 4?
Answer:
IntervalMode option 3 ('Synchronised') forces the agent to synchronize with the system time, ensuring periods begin at the start of the hour. IntervalMode option 4 ('Not synchronised') sets the starting time of the periods to the exact time the agent is enabled and adds the specified interval to this starting time. Both options use a specified interval in minutes to define the duration of each period, but they handle time synchronization differently.

Title: Configuring Accumulator Agents
Topic: Limitations
Question: What is Limitations?
Answer:
The Accumulator Agents allow you to define alarm limits for high and low values. Specifically, you can set the valueHiHi, valueHi, valueLo, and valueLoLo limits, which trigger status bits (VHighHigh, VHigh, VLow, and VLowLow) and associated alarm types when reached. The Low-Low alarm must be on when the Low alarm is on, and the High-High limit will have already been passed when the High limit is reached.

Title: Configuring Accumulator Agents
Topic: Rate of change
Question: What is Rate of change?
Answer:
The agent calculates the rate of change by subtracting the `startValue` from the `inputValue` to determine the differential value of the current period. This differential value is then multiplied by the number of minutes in an hour to calculate the value per hour, which is recorded in the history table.

Title: Configuring Accumulator Agents
Topic: Limitations
Question: What are the limitations of the alarm limits?
Answer:
The alarm limits in the Value alarm levels section of the properties dialog define thresholds for high and low values. Specifically, the valueHiHi alarm limit indicates a second, urgent alarm for high values, the valueLoLo alarm limit represents a second, urgent alarm for low values, and the valueHi and valueLo alarm limits define the first alarm limits for high and low values respectively. These alarms are triggered when a value exceeds or falls below the specified limit, setting corresponding status bits to [1] for alarming.
Category: Classic UI - Agents
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: alarm limits, high value, low value

Title: Configuring Accumulator Agents
Topic: Rate of change
Question: What is Rate of change?
Answer:
Rate of change alarm limits define thresholds for the differential value over a specified period. These limits, including rateHiHi, rateHi, rateLo, and rateLoLo, trigger status bits that can be alarmed using their default alarm types. The deadband slot does not affect these rate alarm limits.
Category: Classic UI - Agents
Document Type: help

Title: Configuring Accumulator Agents
Topic: Rate of change
Question: What is Rate of change?
Answer:
The agent calculates the rate of change of a process variable by subtracting the `startValue` from the `inputValue` to determine the differential value for each period. This differential value is then multiplied by the time elapsed in the period to calculate the value per hour.

Topic: Available column properties:
Question: What column properties are available?
Answer:
Available column properties include DisplayName, BestFit, Width, FormatString, GroupIndex, GroupInterval, SortIndex, and SortOrder. The DisplayName changes the column heading, BestFit determines auto-sizing, Width sets the column width (defaulting to 100 pixels), FormatString specifies data formatting, GroupIndex controls grouping behavior, GroupInterval governs data grouping within the column, SortIndex defines the sorting order, and SortOrder determines the sorting direction (ascending or descending).

Title: Configuring AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer columns

Question: What is Available column properties:?

SummaryType this allows you to perform a calculation on all the entries in this column and display the result of this calculation in the summary row, which the last row at the bottom of the grid. The default is column-specific. - Sum: the summary row displays the total of all the values in this column; - Min: the summary row displays the minimum (lowest) value for this column; - Max: the summary row displays the maximum (highest) value for this column; - Count: the summary row displays the number of items in this column - which is the default setting of the DateTime (DT) column - Average : the summary row displays the average value for this column; - None (the default): no summary calculation is performed on this column's entries SummaryDisplayFormat when a column is calculating a summary, this allows you to specify the required format specifier string for the summary value in {} braces and any descriptive text that should also be displayed.

Title: Configuring how to update AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
The AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control automatically refreshes its contents when new alarms are added, potentially losing any configuration made since the last save. To prevent this, the initial setting is set to 'Ignore' which avoids subscription updates. You can change the update method to 'Prompt' to receive a confirmation dialog for updates, or to 'Auto' to automatically update the control when alarms are added, but 'Auto' should only be used if operators won't be creating filters and searching.

Title: Configuring Pulse Generators
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
Configuration involves setting the Delay time (ms) to specify the period for which the pulse is OFF, and the Pulse width (ms) to determine the ON period of the pulse. The period of the generated pulse is the sum of these two values. The Granularity (ms) field can also be set to specify the monitoring period for time.
Category: Smart UI - Other

Title: Configuring Pulse Generators
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
Configuration involves setting the Delay time (ms) to specify the period for the pulse to be OFF, and the Pulse width (ms) to specify the period for the pulse to be ON. The period is the sum of these two values. The Granularity (ms) field can be used to specify the period for monitoring the time, with a minimum of 100 ms recommended.

Title: Configuring the Notify Agent to send Email messages
Topic: Manually sending email messages
Question: What is manually sending email messages?
Answer:
To manually send email messages with the Notify Agent, create a mimic allowing operators to send emails. You must ensure the agent is not on an alarm route to prevent conflicts with automatic alarms. Configure the Email-To, Email-CC, Email-BC, Email-Subject, Email-Body, and Email-Attachment slots, using commas to separate email addresses and noting that macros are not supported. Setting the BOOLEAN Email-Send-Now slot to '1' triggers the sending process, encapsulating the other email slots into the RAWBYTES Email-rawValue slot for delivery.

Title: Configuring the Shift agent
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
Configuration involves specifying shift patterns for the Shift agent, following a specific order. Special dates must be listed first using the format "yyyy/mm/dd", while day of month entries use the format "mm/dd". Day of week values are disabled when a special date or day of month is specified, and the agent supports a maximum of 6 shifts per day, specifying the last applicable shift time if fewer than 6 are needed.

Title: Control Bits (user modifiable)
Question: What is Control Bits (user modifiable)?
Answer:
Control Bits allow a slot control bit to be set or reset whenever the corresponding agent control bit is set or reset. This fan-out action applies to the raw status value, not to a derived status word, and does not use positive or negative logic.
Category: Smart UI - Security
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: control bits, agent bits, fan-out

---

Title: Control Bits (user modifiable)
Question: What is Control Bits (user modifiable)?
Answer:
Control Bits allow a slot to mirror the state of its corresponding agent bit. When an agent bit is set or reset, the associated slot bits are also set or reset, regardless of their existing state. This behavior is different from Condition Bit fan-in, which utilizes positive or negative logic.
Category: Classic UI - Security
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: control bits, agent bits, slot bits

Title: CreateDumpFiles
Question: What is CreateDumpFiles?
Answer:
CreateDumpFiles creates Agent Server dump (.DMP) files when there is a problem with a WGP file. To enable this feature, set the registry value HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\[Wow6432Node] SOFTWARE Adroit Technologies Adroit Workgroup to 1. To disable dump file creation, set this value to 0.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: dump file, agent server, registry
Source URL: https://ats-adroit.github.io/mysoftware-help/chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/AU_01_02/CreateDumpFiles.htm

Title: CreateDumpFiles
Question: What is CreateDumpFiles?
Answer:
Steps: WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". In order for Adroit to create an Agent Server dump (.DMP) file, which are created when there is a problem with a WGP file, add the following value and set it to 1: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup (REG_)DWORD = 1 To disable the creation of dump files, set this value to 0 the default value.

Title: Creating the Requests collection
Question: What is Creating the Requests collection?
Answer:
Steps: For details, see Steps required to Monitor Real-time Data . One of the objects exposed by the Data Object is the Requests collection, a collection of individual descriptions for required real-time data. Each description consists of a tag (or agent name) plus the names of all the slots to be monitored. The slot names are gathered into another collection called the Properties collection. Since the Data Object provides the Requests collection as one of its properties, the VBA code to gain access to the Requests collection is simply: Set reqs = dataObj.Requests A single request consists of the tag plus the names of all slots to be monitored.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: procedural
Keywords: collection, smart, requests, adroit scada, adroit, html, creating the requests collection, smart ui - other, the, creating, ui

Title: Creating the Requests collection
Question: What is Creating the Requests collection?

Title: Custom Agent Usage Guidelines
Question: What is Custom Agent Usage Guidelines?
Answer:
The Custom Agent Usage Guidelines recommend monitoring the virtual memory and CPU usage of the AS.EXE (Agent Server) process during design and commissioning to ensure optimal performance. Specifically, for 32-bit operating systems, if virtual memory exceeds 1.0 GB, convert to C++ agents; and for 64-bit systems, if memory exceeds 2.0 GB, convert to C++ agents. Also, ensure code is optimized and that only necessary slots are output enabled to avoid scan degradation.
Category: Smart UI - Agents
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: custom agent, agent server, memory usage, CPU usage, C++ agent

Title: Data Element spiders
Question: What is Data Element spiders?
Answer:
A Data Element spider is a component that connects data elements—typically values or properties from a graphic form—to other data elements or data sources. It functions automatically when you drag a data element from a datasource onto a graphic form or another spider, or can be manually created as a placeholder for a data element, particularly when unavailable. These spiders use namespaces (e.g., ServerName.datasourceName.dataElementName) to define their relationships and are triggered by events or silks.

Title: Data Execution Prevention (DEP) Configuration
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
Steps: Data Execution Prevention (DEP) prevents damage from viruses and other security threats that attack by running (executing) malicious code from memory locations that only Windows and other programs should use. However, when this is NOT configured to use the default setting (typically this occurs on Windows Server 2003 although can occur on other operating systems that provide this such as Windows XP etc.), then the Agent Server can become unable to read the HASP at start up, which will cause the Agent Server to hang or fail and/or to display HASP exceptions in the Agent Server window.

Title: Data Execution Prevention (DEP) Configuration
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
Configuration refers to Data Execution Prevention (DEP), which prevents malicious code from running from memory locations intended for programs. To ensure Adroit functions correctly, check DEP settings: the default setting is "Turn on DEP for essential Windows programs and service only", but if you experience issues, enable DEP for all programs and services except those you select and add the AS.EXE and ASS.EXE executables from the Adroit installation folder (typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit) to the DEP list.

Question: What is Analogue Data Links?
Answer:
Analogue Data Links display statistics for floating-point process variables (PVs) calculated over a rolling time period. These links show the PV value, its units, and the average value calculated over that period. Clicking on the link reveals additional statistics like the maximum, minimum, and deviation values, which are initially 0 until the statsPeriod is configured, typically to 10 minutes.

Title: Data Logging Compression Methods
Question: What is Data Logging Compression Methods?
Answer:
Data logging compression methods reduce the number of log records by specifying a time and value deadband in the Datalog agent. This means a value is only logged if its change exceeds the deadband, and the logging method (Average, Minimum, Maximum, or) uses the specified Time deadband to determine which value is logged. The Average method is recommended as it calculates a time-weighted average of all changes within the deadband period, providing a more accurate representation of the data compared to raw log values.
Category: Smart UI - Logging
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: logging, compression, deadband, Datalog
Source URL: https://ats-adroit.github.io/mysoftware-help/chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/AU_01_08/Data_Logging_Compression_Methods.htm
Source File: chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/AU_01_08/Data_Logging_Compression_Methods.htm

---

Title: Data Logging Compression Methods
Question: What is Data Logging Compression Methods?
Answer:
Data logging compression methods reduce the number of log records by specifying a time and value deadband in the Datalog agent. This means a value is only logged if its change exceeds the deadband, or if multiple changes occur within the deadband period, using algorithms like average, minimum, maximum, or the time-weighted average. The average method is recommended for a more accurate representation of data trends.

Title: Data Specification Method for Statistical Agent
Topic: Specifications
Question: What is Specifications?
Answer:
The Statistical Agent uses a method called STREAMING to collect data, which combines all collected input values into a single sample for analysis. This sample is created from individual STREAM EVENTS, which represent input values collected on an event basis. The agent then calculates statistical data like maximum, minimum, average, and standard deviation for this combined sample.

Title: Data Structure of an Agent
Question: What is Data Structure of an Agent?
Answer:
Agents contain multiple data items called agent attributes, accessible to clients as slots. An agent's state is defined by the collective values of all its data, which includes both generic and type-specific slots. Generic slots, such as agentDescription and status, are common to all agents, while type-specific slots, like rawValue and value, are unique to particular agent types.
Category: Smart UI - Agents
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: agent, attributes, slots, data

Title: Data Structure of an Agent
Question: What is Data Structure of an Agent?
Answer:
Agents are designed to contain multiple data items called agent attributes, accessible to clients as slots. An agent's state is defined as the collective values of all its data, which includes both generic and type-specific slots. Type-specific slots, like rawValue and value, are specific to the agent type, such as the Analog agent.

Title: Date and Time formatting syntax
Question: What is Date and Time formatting syntax?
Answer:
Date and Time formatting syntax uses format specifiers like '%f', 'gg', 'hh', 'hhh', 'h', 'hh', 'H', 'mmm', and 'm' to specify how dates and times are displayed. The 'f' format specifier produces a long date and short time format. The 'g' format specifier produces a general format, while 'hh' and 'H' display hours in the range 1-12 or 0-23, respectively, with leading zeros if needed.

Title: Date Format Flag
Question: What is Date Format Flag?
Answer:
The Date Format Flag, denoted by '#', can be used to prefix formatting code characters after the '%' symbol. When used with %#c, it produces a long date and time representation appropriate for the current locale, such as "Tuesday, March 16, 1993, 12:41:29". When used with %#x, it generates a long date representation appropriate to the current locale, such as "Tuesday, March 16, 1993".

Title: DbAccess Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Slots:
Question: What is Slots?
Answer:
Slots are configuration settings within the DbAccess Agent that track transaction activity. The `badTransactions` and `goodTransactions` slots increment based on successful or unsuccessful transactions, respectively, and are reset to 0 upon Agent Server restarts. Other slots, like `connectionString`, `dbRowCriteria`, and `dbSQL`, define the database connection and transaction parameters.
Category: Smart UI - Agents
Document Type: help

Title: DbAccess Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Specifications
Question: What is Specifications?
Answer:
The DbAccess Agent's status bits provide information about the connection and transaction state. Specifically, bit 16 indicates a disconnected state, bit 17 indicates a connected state, bit 18 signals a transaction error, and bit 19 indicates an overrun error when a scheduled transaction exceeds its time limit. Bit 20 indicates a connection error, and bit 21 indicates a transaction success.

Title: Default Alarm Management Queries
Question: What is Default Alarm Management Queries?
Answer:
Default Alarm Management Queries provide metrics related to alarm activity, including burst rate (calculated as 6 times the maximum alarm count in a 10-minute period), percent upset (calculated based on alarms per hour), priority distribution, standing alarms, and most frequent alarms. These queries are designed to measure alarm system usability and operator response capabilities, with typical ranges and thresholds varying by industry standards.

Title: Demand Logging
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
The Datalog agent uses three slots: LogNow, Trigger, and Mode to control logging behavior. LogNow logs transitions from 0 to 1 to disk, Trigger allows you to monitor a tag for a zero-to-non-zero transition, and Mode controls the logging mode (Normal, Demand-based, or Demand and Change-based).

Title: Demand Logging
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
Steps: Use the following three slots of the Datalog agent: Slot Type Description LogNow BOOLEAN The current value is logged to disk every time this slot makes the transition from 0 to 1. Trigger STRING An optional tag (agent.slot) configuration which is monitored for a zero to non-zero transition. When this occurs, a log will take place. Mode INTEGER A variable to control the mode of operation as follows: - Normal – change based logging only - Demand based logging only - Demand and change based logging If necessary, you can ALSO use the Datalog compression algorithm when using , by configuring the Support compression algorithm on global datalogging setting.

Title: Demand Scanning
Topic: What is demand scanning and how should it be used?
Question: What is demand scanning and how should it be used??
Answer:
Demand scanning, also known as New Adroit Scanning Architecture, is a protocol optimized for NASA that reduces the communication of process values when they are only being read and displayed, such as on a mimic or graphic form. It's used to minimize data transfer costs, particularly over networks like GSM or satellite communications, and to improve network throughput. Demand scanning only applies to read-only process values that are displayed or used by graphic forms.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: demand scanning, NASA, process values, mimic

Title: Demand Scanning
Topic: What is demand scanning and how should it be used?
Question: What is demand scanning and how should it be used??
Answer:
Demand scanning is a mechanism that optimizes system performance by only scanning process values that benefit from it. Do not configure process values that will never utilize this mechanism, such as those logged or alarmed, as this can lead to slower system performance without any benefits.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: demand scanning, process values, optimization

Title: Demand Scanning
Topic: Usage scenarios NOT recommended for demand scanning:
Question: What is Usage scenarios NOT recommended for demand scanning:?
Answer:
Demand scanning is not recommended for process values that are being alarmed, actively logged, or used by another Adroit agent. Specifically, it should not be used with an 'Output Enabled' scanning setting, nor with clustered Agent Servers using shadow scanning and a proxy server, as these configurations can lead to incorrect values and system performance degradation. Utilizing 'demand scanning' for a clustered Agent Server that uses shadow scanning and a proxy server to handle requests for its tags from remote clients could return INCORRECT VALUEs.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: demand scanning, agent server, shadow scanning, proxy server

Configuration involves enabling a global setting checkbox on the Driver Configuration page within the Config Editor, accessed through the Advanced Driver Options button. The demandScanningEnabled slot in the Device agent is enabled when the device’s protocol driver supports New Adroit Scanning Architecture (NASA).

The SmartUI Server can handle up to 5 clients connecting over the Internet and up to 10 clients over the LAN. Title: Deployment considerations
Topic: Network topology used for Client connections:
Question: What is Network topology used for Client connections?
Answer:
Network topology determines how Clients connect to Servers, with the most common options being the LAN or the Internet. By default, the SmartUI Launcher can deploy and update applications using the selected topology, and it's recommended that only the SmartUI Operator application connects to the Server over the Internet unless a high bandwidth connection is available. The Designer requires a two-way data flow and needs to connect over the Internet as well.

Title: Desubscribe ActiveX Method
Question: What is Desubscribe ActiveX Method?
Answer:
The Desubscribe method removes a subscription from a previously subscribed tag. It takes a SubscriptionHandle as input, which was previously returned by the Subscribe or SubscribeBulk methods. The method returns TRUE on success and FALSE if an error occurs, with LastError/LastErrorNum providing details about the failure.

Title: Device Agent - Database File Format
Question: What is Device Agent - Database File Format?
Answer:
The Device Agent - Database File Format (WGP file) contains a binary dump of the device's registry configuration. This allows for portability between computers, automatically creating the device entry if it’s not found in the registry. The file includes configuration settings such as DRV (protocol driver DLL name), RLN (binary dump size in bytes), and REG (the binary dump itself), as well as subscription and scanning specifications.

The Device Agent Database File Format (WGP file) contains a binary dump of the device's registry configuration. Question: What is Device Management Settings?
Answer:
Device Management Settings allow an SNMPMgr to manage a single device by retrieving and/or setting and/or trapping its SNMP managed object data. This data includes device configuration parameters, performance statistics, and operational data. To enable device management, you must enable polling, specify a poll rate (in milliseconds), and configure the number of OID values per polling transaction.

Title: DisableADOTableNamePrefix
Question: What is DisableADOTableNamePrefix?
Answer:
The `DisableADOTableNamePrefix` setting removes the "AdroitRawLog_" table name prefix that Adroit creates when logging to a single OLE DB table. To disable this, set the registry value `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\[Wow6432Node]SOFTWARE\[Adroit Technologies]\[Adroit]\[Logging]` to 1.
Category: Smart UI - Other

Title: Displays
Topic: Analogue Displays
Question: What is Analogue Displays?
Answer:
Analogue Displays are rectangles with a light grey background that display the value of an associated analogue (floating point) process variable (PV). They show the PV value in black, the unit of measurement if specified, and an alarm priority indication when an associated alarm bit is present. These displays require mandatory specification of the value slot, unit slot, and alarm priority slot when added to a graphic form.

Title: Displays
Topic: Analogue Displays
Question: What is Analogue Displays?
Answer:
Analogue Displays are process variable (PV) values that display alarm priorities based on their assigned levels. These priorities, ranging from Lowest (Royal Blue - Priority 0) to Highest (Red - Priority 4), are indicated by color (Magenta, Orange, Yellow, Red) when applicable. Title: Dual mode tags
Question: What is Dual mode tags?
Answer:
Dual mode tags are tags added to both control groups and normal groups to ensure tag values are updated across Agent Servers. The order of group definitions – normal group above control group – prioritizes updates to the local Agent Server from the remote Agent Server. Alternatively, defining the normal group below the control group designates the client Agent Server as the master for the tag, sending the tag value first.
Category: Classic UI - Configuration
Document Type: configuration
Section Type: configuration
Keywords: dual mode tags, tag groups, Agent Server

Title: EnableUnchangedValueWrites
Question: What is EnableUnchangedValueWrites?
Answer:
The `EnableUnchangedValueWrites` registry value controls whether Adroit sends an output to a PLC regardless of changes to the rawvalue slot of the Digital agent. Setting this value to 1 will send an output, while the default value of 0 only sends an output when the rawvalue slot changes. This setting is used in conjunction with Operator Action Behaviours.

---

Title: EnvisaLinkTPI-1-08
Topic: 1.0 Overview
Question: How do I configure 1.0 Overview in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The EnvisaLink TPI allows third-party command and control applications to interface with the EnvisaLink module and security system over a TCP/IP connection. To initiate a connection, the application must establish a TCP socket and send a 005 login request containing the session status command (505) and password. The EnvisaLink listens on port 4025 and will close the connection if the password is not received within 10 seconds or if the password fails.
Category: Drivers
Document Type: driver
Section Type: driver
Keywords: EnvisaLink TPI, TCP connection, session password, port 4025

Answer:
The Envisalink TPI connection will continue until dropped due to network disruptions or exceptions. To test the connection, use the Poll command (000), which is issued by the panel every 4 minutes, or monitor the period time broadcast (510).

Title: EnvisaLinkTPI-1-08
Topic: 3.1 Communications Protocol
Question: How do I configure 3.1 Communications Protocol in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Steps: All data is sent as hex ASCII codes. The transmission from will consist of the following: CCC DDD…DDD CKS CR/LF CCC => 3 Digit Command This tells the module or the application what to do. Commands are 3 characters long. For example, the Status Command (001) would be sent as hex ASCII codes ‘30 30 31’. See the following tables for a list of supported commands. DDD…DDD => Data Byte(s) This is the data that may be needed for the command.

Title: Evaluation Options for Expressions
Question: What is Evaluation Options for Expressions?
Answer:
There are two options available: evaluate expressions continuously or only when triggered by a change in the trigger input slot. When continuous evaluation is selected, a new result is generated whenever any of the inputs change or the expression itself changes. To avoid unnecessary CPU loads and network traffic, you can disable subscription updates by adding the PropagateTrigger registry value.

The file format uses tags to identify source agents and slots for input.

Running time is the time a process or machine is actively running, determined by the OEE agent's BOOLEAN 'running' slot. The agent increments this slot when the 'running' tag is ON, and it's influenced by the active state of the 'input1' slot, which measures production.

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: Complex mode and KPI calculation
Question: What is Complex mode and KPI calculation?
Answer:
Complex mode in the OEE agent allows for KPI calculations that involve two measurements instead of just time. When Complex mode is enabled, the KPI% is calculated by dividing the Total for the Shift for input1 by the Total for the Shift for input2, both divided by the Target KPI. However, note that OEE agents operating in complex mode cannot calculate OEE.

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: OEE calculations
Question: What is OEE calculations?
Answer:
OEE% is calculated using the formula: OEE% = Quality% * Performance% * Availability%. Quality% measures the number of good parts produced relative to total parts produced, Performance% measures the actual production rate against the designed capacity, and Availability% measures the uptime of the equipment.
Category: Smart UI - Scripting
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: OEE, KPI, Quality, Performance, Availability

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: Quality factor
Question: What is Quality factor?
Answer:
The Quality factor, calculated by the OEE agent, is determined by dividing the number of rejects by the total number of items produced during a shift. This percentage (ranging from 0 to 100) must be driven externally, with a default value of 100%.

Running time is the time a process or machine is actively producing, as determined by the BOOLEAN 'running' slot in the OEE agent. The agent increments this slot when the 'running' slot is ON, but it expects the 'available' slot to also be ON. If the 'available' slot is OFF, runtime will continue to increment, even if availability is down.

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: Available time
Question: What is Available time?
Answer:
Whereas KPI calculations are performed against runtime, OEE calculations are calculated against the time that the process/machine is available for production. The OEE agent therefore uses the BOOLEAN available slot (or the optional BOOLEAN tag reference availableTag ) to determine the maximum . - This slot should be ON when the machine/process is supposed to be running.

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: Complex mode and KPI calculation
Question: What is Complex mode and KPI calculation?
Answer:
Complex mode in the OEE agent is enabled when the Input type 2 field (the type2 slot) is set to something other than Unused (0). When in complex mode, the KPI% is calculated by dividing the total for the shift for input1 by the total for the shift for input2, both divided by the target KPI. Normal OEE and KPI calculations do not use the Input 2 field, and the input type is set to Unused (0).
Category: Classic UI - Scripting
Document Type: help

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: OEE calculations
Question: What is OEE calculations?
Answer:
OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) is calculated using the formula: OEE% = Quality% * Performance% * Availability%. Quality% measures the percentage of good parts produced, Performance% measures the output compared to design capacity, and Availability% measures the uptime of the equipment.
Category: Classic UI - Scripting
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: OEE, KPI, Quality, Performance, Availability
Source URL: https://ats-adroit.github.io/mysoftware-help/chm_extracted/Classic_UI/adroit/AU_01_05/Factors_affecting_OEE_or_KPI_calculations.htm
Source File: chm_extracted/Classic_UI/adroit/AU_01_05/Factors_affecting_OEE_or_KPI_calculations.htm

---

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: Quality factor
Question: What is Quality factor?
Answer:
The Quality factor, used in OEE calculations, is determined by multiplying reject and total counts for the shift. This value, expressed as a percentage, must be driven externally and defaults to 100%.
Category: Classic UI - Scripting
Document Type: help

It takes an agent slot, start time, end time, and the number of samples as input parameters, returning an OLE Automation VARIANT structure with date/time and interpolated value data. The function will fail if the number of samples exceeds 9999 and cannot retrieve values of type STRING.
