Title: Scanning Interval Configuration Tips
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
The scanning interval, specified in the Scan rate (ms) field, determines the time in milliseconds before a tag's value is communicated to or from a FED device (like a PLC or RTU) during scanning. This setting is crucial for polled devices and should be configured to minimize queueing of tasks created by Adroit, ensuring configuration tasks (like adding/removing scan points) are processed efficiently. Longer scan intervals reduce task queue size, allowing for quicker handling of configuration tasks and control actions.
Category: Smart UI - Configuration
Document Type: configuration
Section Type: configuration
Keywords: scanning interval, scan rate, polling, FED device
Source URL: https://ats-adroit.github.io/mysoftware-help/chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/AU_01_06/Scanning_Interval_Configuration_Tips.htm

Title: Scanning Interval Configuration Tips
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
Configuration involves setting up the scan interval to prevent issues with data polling from multiple RTU devices. This ensures that the driver doesn't lose synchronization due to delays in responses from RTU devices, which can occur if they respond at different speeds.

Title: Scanning Optimization
Question: What is Scanning Optimization?
Answer:
The optimization of scanning the process of communicating a value (slot), typically to and/or from a front-end device (FED). typically involves grouping data correctly within front-end devices, so as to prevent fragmentation of the data that usually creates a bottleneck for communication performance. Usually I/Os acquired from the plant are not needed by the SCADA, but are intermingled with the SCADA I/O.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: general
Keywords: smart, scanning, optimization, adroit scada, adroit, other, scanning optimization, html, smart ui - other, ui
Source URL: https://ats-adroit.github.io/mysoftware-help/chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/AU_01_06/Scanning_Optimization.htm
Source File: chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/AU_01_06/Scanning_Optimization.htm

---

Title: Scanning Optimization
Question: What is Scanning Optimization?
Answer:
Scanning optimization is the process of communicating data values (slots) from a front-end device to prevent data fragmentation and communication bottlenecks. This involves grouping data by data type (e.g., Analog and Digital) and scan rate, allocating separate memory space for SCADA tags and internal I/O, and leveraging addressable data blocks if available from front-end devices like Siemens controllers. Optimizing scan times is recommended, especially for Digital data, to avoid communication errors and control sending issues.
Category: Classic UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: scanning, optimization, data grouping, front-end device, scan rate
Source URL: https://ats-adroit.github.io/mysoftware-help/chm_extracted/Classic_UI/adroit/AU_01_06/Scanning_Optimization.htm
Source File: chm_extracted/Classic_UI/adroit/AU_01_06/Scanning_Optimization.htm

Title: Scanning Tags Using Contiguous Addresses
Topic: To scan a number of tags to continuous addresses in the same device:
Question: What is To scan a number of tags to continuous addresses in the same device?
Answer:
To scan a number of tags to continuous addresses in the same device, first create a scanning template by scanning the first tag to the first address of the range. Then, ensure the 'Stopped' option is selected in the scanning dialog to stop the device, and finally, click the 'Scan...' button or right-click to add the selected tags to the device using the pre-configured scanning parameters.

Title: Scanning Tags Using Contiguous Addresses
Topic: To scan a number of tags to continuous addresses in the same device:
Question: What is To scan a number of tags to continuous addresses in the same device?
Answer:
To scan a number of tags to continuous addresses in the same device, first create a scanning template by scanning the first tag at the first address of the desired range. This involves specifying the agent type, slot, device, starting address, scan rate, and deadband, and optionally setting output enable and scan inhibit bits. Then, select the agents by dragging the mouse or holding CTRL and clicking in the Agent list to add the selected tags to the device.

Question: What is Scanning-issue Checklist before Contacting Support?
Answer:
Before contacting support regarding scanning issues with Adroit, check several items to attempt self-resolution. Also, confirm the Agent Server type is set to 'Cluster server' in the Adroit Setup utility and note the Project Name and Agent Server Name, along with checking the Connection tab for Standby mode.

Title: ScanTag ActiveX Method
Question: What is ScanTag ActiveX Method?
Answer:
The ScanTag ActiveX Method configures a tag for scanning within Adroit. It uses putslot functionality internally and requires the Agent Server to be licensed with a HASP key or run under a Limited Time License. This method allows you to scan a fully qualified named value (agentName.slotName) at a specified rate and deadband, and can also be used to unscan an item by specifying a negative rate.

Title: ScanTag ActiveX Method
Question: What is ScanTag ActiveX Method?
Answer:
The ScanTag ActiveX method configures a tag, represented as a fully qualified named value (agentName.slotName), for scanning. It uses putslot functionality internally and requires either a licensed Agent Server with a HASP key or a Limited Time License HASP to operate. The method takes parameters such as AgentOrSlot, Slot, Device, Address, Rate, DeadBand, and OutputEnable to control the scanning process.

The Scheduler Agent database file format uses a WGP file with specific slots to define schedule parameters. Title: Scheduler Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Slots:
Question: What is Slots?
Answer:
Slots define scheduled periods within a Scheduler agent. These periods determine when the agent's value is calculated. Key slots include `datesToExclude`, `recDaysOfWeek`, `recDaysOfMonth`, `recEndDate`, and `recIndex` which allow you to configure specific dates, days, and time ranges for the agent to execute.

Title: Scheduler Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Slots:
Question: What is Slots?
Answer:
Slots define the specific time schedules for an agent. Each slot includes a start datetime, end datetime, weekdays, day of month, last day of month, and a special flag to control deletion when the end datetime is reached. The uct parameter determines whether times are specified in UTC or local time.

Title: Scheduler Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Slots:
Question: What is Slots?
Answer:
Slots define the schedule for a Scheduler Agent, specifying when and how the agent should execute. They control the parameters for the scheduled period, including dates to exclude, the executable program to run, and the end date/time. The 'enabled' setting determines if the scheduled period determines the agent's value, or if it can be manually controlled.

Title: Scheduler Agent - Slot Details

Answer:
Slots define the start and end times for a schedule record. Each slot contains a 'Start datetime' and 'End datetime' parameter, along with options for specifying weekdays, the day of the month, and whether the entry is valid only on the last day of the month. The 'uct' parameter determines whether times are specified in UTC or local time.

Title: Scheduling and Triggering Scripts
Question: What is Scheduling and Triggering Scripts?
Answer:
Scheduling and triggering scripts allows the remote execution of the main subroutine by the Script agent. This functionality offers several configurations: triggering only based on tag changes, scheduling execution at a set time, or a combination of both triggered events and scheduled times. It’s important to note that errors in scripts will be logged, and the event log should be monitored for potential flooding.

Document Type: help

Title: Script Agent - Database File Format
Question: What is Script Agent - Database File Format?
Answer:
The Script Agent database file format utilizes a series of fields to define agent behavior and module references. Specifically, it includes fields like IDX, IVL, LSTn, BAR, EID, EVT, ML, SM, SI, SF, TE, TL, and TRG# which define index pointers, string descriptions, list identifiers, module locations, script engine identifiers, event log error counts, module lists, subroutine names, trigger enabled states, and trigger lists, respectively.

Title: Script Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Specifications
Question: What is Specifications?
Answer:
The Script Agent has several status bits that indicate the state of the agent and its scripts. Specifically, bit 16 indicates the Idle State, which is on when no script is running, and bit 17 indicates the Running State when a script is executing. Additionally, bits 18, 19, and 20 represent Compilation error, Runtime error, and Overrun error states, respectively.

Title: Secondary Port Disabled
Question: What is Secondary Port Disabled?
Answer:
A device enters recovery mode if a Read or Write transaction fails. This process involves Adroit requesting an update from the front-end device, a timeout phase, and a retry phase if the response is invalid. The scanning will resume immediately if the retries are exhausted.
Category: Smart UI - Other

Title: Secondary Port Disabled
Question: What is Secondary Port Disabled?
Answer:
A device enters recovery mode when a Read or Write transaction fails, triggering a three-step process: the driver requests an update from the front-end device, times out if there's no response, and retries the request a configured number of times. If all retries fail, the scanning process immediately resumes.

Title: Secondary Port Enabled
Question: What is Secondary Port Enabled?
Answer:
Secondary Port Enabled allows Adroit to utilize a separate port if communications with the primary hardware component fail. This involves a port switchover, and only occurs once during a transaction to recover from Read or Write transaction failures, ensuring continued operation with the primary hardware if the secondary port also fails.

Title: Security configuration
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
The SmartUI security system utilizes a configurable subset of existing Windows users and groups – known as "allowed" users and groups – to provide foundational security and user management. These allowed users and groups are mandatory for every Server and grant specific users and groups total or global security access to the Server, recommended for security administration. To further secure access, users may be configured to use impersonated user names and passwords, preventing login without being an allowed user or group member.

Title: Select queries
Question: What is Select queries?
Answer:
Select queries are used to manage your database connected to an OLE DB datasource and allow you to select a subset of data tailored to specific needs. These queries define relationships between fields and include criteria that must be met by values in those fields, and can be parameterized for flexibility. Unlike tables, Select queries display all records matching specified criteria and can be queued to prevent data loss if the connection fails.

Title: Server clustering
Topic: SmartUI Server clustering
Question: What is SmartUI Server clustering?
Answer:
SmartUI Servers can be clustered to provide load balancing and redundancy. Cluster partners (SmartUI Servers within a cluster) must have identical configurations, including server name, server configuration, system time, and Microsoft Windows security configuration. Additionally, users must be able to log in to all cluster partners with the same credentials and all cluster partners must be in the same network domain or workgroup. Only one Server can run on a specific machine at any point in time.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: clustering, SmartUI Server, load balancing, redundancy, cluster partners
Source URL: https://ats-adroit.github.io/mysoftware-help/chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/05Dply/50Cfg/Server_clustering.htm
Source File: chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/05Dply/50Cfg/Server_clustering.htm

---

Title: Server clustering
Topic: SmartUI Server clustering
Question: What is SmartUI Server clustering?
Answer:
SmartUI Server clustering allows SmartUI Operators to maintain a list of available SmartUI Servers and automatically switch to the server with the lightest load. Cluster-aware SmartUI Operators obtain Server availability and load information through UDP broadcasts, and the default UDP port range for these broadcasts is 11000-11010. It's crucial to update the BroadcastPortRange setting on the Server and Client if you change the port range.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: clustering, SmartUI Server, broadcast, UDP ports

Title: Shift Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Specifications
Question: What is Specifications?
Answer:
Shift Agent slot specifications include status bits that provide information about the shift operation. Specifically, bit 16, 'ShiftEnd', is pulsed at the end of every shift to enable shift end operations, while bit 17, 'InvalidShift', is active when the shift pattern entry is not found. Bit 18, 'ConnectionError', is on if the OLEDB connection string is invalid.

Title: Siemens Ethernet 1st Generation ISO-TCP
Topic: Overview
Question: How do I configure Overview in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Adroit supports the Siemens Ethernet protocol via ISO over TCP/IP for S7-200/300/400 PLCs. To configure this, use MicroWin version 4.0 with the appropriate CP card (CP 243-1, CP343-1, or CP443-1) and ensure the Destination TSAP CPU and Rack positions are set to 2. Additionally, the system requires no other drivers, stacks, or PLC code, provided the CP card is configured with an appropriate Ethernet address and mask.

Title: SIMPDRV - Adroit Simulation Protocol Driver
Topic: Automatically Incrementing Scanned SIMPLC Values:
Question: What is Automatically Incrementing Scanned SIMPLC Values?
Answer:
The SIMPLC values are automatically incremented by the DB number for each scan, following the formula: newvalue = oldvalue + DBnumber. This means DB 0 will never increment, while a scan with DB100:DW### will increment the value by 100.

Title: Situational Awareness (or High Performance SCADA)
Question: What is Situational Awareness (or High Performance SCADA)?
Answer:
This is a minimalistic standard of user interface design, which has come about through years of research and trial and error. This standard moves away from the brightly colored and the almost photo-realistic process design of the past which used bright colors that while at the outset were visually appealing, proved in practice to only distract the operators from the process they were monitoring.

Title: size Behaviours
Question: What is size Behaviours?
Answer:
Size Behaviors dynamically resize controls and graphic elements (vectors) based on a monitored value. You define a minimum and maximum value for the monitored value, and the object will scale linearly when the value reaches its maximum, magnifying width and/or height by a specified factor. The object retains its original size when the monitored value is less than or equal to the minimum value.

Title: size Behaviours
Question: What is size Behaviours?
Answer:
Size Behaviors adjust the size of objects (like controls or vectors) when the associated Input Data Element value reaches its maximum. This scaling is controlled by a multiplier, which can increase the width and/or height of the object, and is defined in pixels. The behavior dictates whether the object expands from the left corner, uses anchor points to control the expansion direction, or utilizes the vector's center point.

Title: Slot Status Words
Question: What is Slot Status Words?
Answer:
Slot Status Words provide a granular view of an agent's status, mirroring the overall agent status but offering more detailed monitoring and control. These words, accessed by appending 'status' to the slot name (e.g., ANA01.status), are based on bit allocations and meanings identical to the overall agent status. The statusBad bit is the only bit an application needs to monitor for agent or slot integrity.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help

Slot Status Words provide a detailed status for each slot within an agent, offering improved monitoring and control. This feature utilizes the same bit allocations and meanings as the overall agent status, allowing you to monitor the integrity of the agent or slot using the statusBit00 bit.

Title: SmartInhibit
Question: What is SmartInhibit?
Answer:
SmartInhibit is a registry setting that controls how the alarming subsystem treats alarms when the agent’s statusalarmInhibit slot is set to one. Specifically, you can configure it to either clear the alarm with reported data set to "Inhibited" (setting = 1) or show the alarm as not active (setting = 2).
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help

Title: SmartInhibit
Question: What is SmartInhibit?
Answer:
SmartInhibit is a registry setting that controls how the alarming subsystem treats current alarms when the agent’s statusalarmInhibit slot is set to one. Specifically, setting this value to 0 prevents any changes to the alarm state, 1 clears the alarm and sets reported data to "Inhibited", and 2 clears the alarm and sets reported data to "Inhibited", making the alarm appear inactive.

Title: SNMP Community Strings
Question: What is SNMP Community Strings?
Answer:
SNMP community strings act like usernames and passwords, providing specific access to data from SNMP-managed devices, such as hardware configurations and performance statistics. There are three types: Read-only, Read-Write, and Trap, each with distinct uses and limitations. Up to 16 community strings can be defined per device, and it’s common for devices to have unique sets for simplified network management.

Title: SNMP Managed Objects
Question: What is SNMP Managed Objects?
Answer:
SNMP Managed Objects are data exposed by network devices that use SNMP Simple Network Management Protocol to monitor and manage these devices. These objects, described in the SNMP Management Information Base (MIB), include hardware, configuration parameters, and performance statistics, and are uniquely identified using Object Identifiers (OIDs).

Answer:
Steps: Network devices that are managed by SNMP Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is used to monitor and manage a diverse range of devices on a computer network. expose their management data as managed objects. These managed objects might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and so on, that directly relate to the current operation of the device. Title: SNMP Object Value Return Types
Question: What is SNMP Object Value Return Types?
Answer:
SNMP object values can return data in several types, including Integer32, Unsigned 32-bit value, 32-bit counter, 32-bit gauge, Time ticks, 64-bit counter, Real, String, Bits, Object Identifier, and Sequence. Each type has a recommended agent (typically Real or String) and indicates whether the data can be written to. Only Integer32, Unsigned 32-bit value, 32-bit counter, 32-bit gauge, Time ticks, 64-bit counter, and Real are writable.

Title: SNMPManager Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Slots:
Question: What is Slots?:
Answer:
The SNMPManager Agent populates trap slots with information about traps in the queue, reducing the trapCount slot. Once a trap is read from the queue, it is discarded and cannot be accessed again. This agent uses a work queue to prevent corruption of the main trap queue when processing sub-traps.

Title: SNMPManager Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Specifications
Question: What is Specifications?
Answer:
The SNMPManager Agent uses status bits to indicate its connection status and operational state. Specifically, status bit 16 indicates an inability to access the device, status bit 17 indicates the agent is connected but not receiving OID values, status bit 18 indicates the agent is connected and receiving OID values, and status bit 19 indicates the agent is unlicensed. Status bit 20 indicates the hierarchical tree of Available Objects (OIDs) is being fetched, and status bit 21 indicates a non-connection related error.

Title: SNMPManager Agent Usage Requirements
Topic: Requirements
Question: What are the requirements for using the SNMPManager agent?
Answer:
The SNMPManager agent requires several conditions to be met before monitoring network devices. First, each device must have a single, fixed IP address, and the agent cannot manage multiple devices simultaneously. Second, the device must be accessible on the network and the SNMP service should only be run on devices you intend to monitor. Finally, security settings must allow SNMP traffic on UDP port 161, and an appropriate OEM license is required to monitor two or more devices.

The 'slots' value within the SNMPMgr Agent represents a work queue used to prevent corruption of the main trap queue when handling sub-traps. This queue processes sub-traps from the main trap queue, ensuring data integrity.

Title: SNMPMgr Agent Usage Requirements
Topic: Requirements
Question: What is Requirements?
Answer:
The SNMPMgr agent requires several key conditions to operate effectively. First, each device you want to monitor must have a unique IP address or port address to avoid conflicts, and the device must be accessible on the network (pingable). Additionally, you must know the SNMP version supported by the device, and you may need to install and configure the Windows SNMP service if monitoring a computer.

Title: SNMPMgr Agent Usage Requirements
Topic: Requirements
Question: What is Requirements?
Answer:
The SNMPMgr Agent requires an available scan license for each unique OID (Object Identifier) polled, written to, or trapped from the device. If the agent requires more scan licenses than available, all OID operations are disabled, and an error status is set. You also need the device's community string with appropriate read/write or read-only rights to monitor or control it.

Title: SNMPMgr Agent Usage Requirements
Topic: Requirements
Question: What are the requirements for using the SNMPMgr agent?
Answer:
The SNMPMgr agent requires a device with a single, fixed IP address or a unique port address for unique identification. The device must be accessible on the network (able to be pinged), and you must know the SNMP version supported by the device, along with its connection settings. Additionally, SNMP traffic must be allowed through any firewalls, typically UDP port 161. For monitoring multiple devices, a separate OEM license is required.

Title: Strike EnerMAX
Topic: Overview
Question: How do I configure Overview in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
To configure Overview in Adroit SCADA, you must set the Baud rate to 300 for the optical interface or 2400 if using the remote RS-232/485 connection. The Comms Speed is the speed the driver changes to after connecting, and the Retry value determines how many times Adroit will attempt communication before failing. The Network/port Idle time applies to all Reads and Writes out to the meter.

Title: SubsWriteTimeout
Question: What is SubsWriteTimeout?
Answer:
SubsWriteTimeout is a registry setting that forces the Agent Server to timeout if the network channel between the client and server fills up due to high CPU load or other issues. To prevent this, set the value to 100 milliseconds in the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\[Wow6432Node]\[SOFTWARE]\[Adroit Technologies]\[Adroit]\[Workgroup]\[WG.INI registry key.

Title: SubsWriteTimeout
Question: What is SubsWriteTimeout?
Answer:
SubsWriteTimeout is a registry setting used to force the Agent Server to timeout if the network channel between a slow client and the server becomes overloaded. Setting this value to 100 milliseconds (REG_DWORD = 100) can prevent the Agent Server from failing due to high CPU load or network congestion.

Answer:
This setting, found in the WG.INI registry value, allows you to change output enabled process values to Agent Server values on startup. It is set by adding the DWORD value 'REG_DWORD = 1' to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\WG.INI. However, you must also use the Forceoutputs setting and the scan inhibit setting simultaneously when using this option.

Title: SystemDataLog Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Specifications
Question: What is Specifications?
Answer:
The SystemDataLog Agent utilizes status bits to indicate the state of its data catchup process. Specifically, bit 16 indicates when the datalog catchup is complete, bit 17 indicates when the process is in progress, bit 18 indicates a failure, bit 19 indicates a low catchup rate, and bit 20 indicates a backup process is active. Bit 21 signals an error during the last datalog backup.

Title: Temporarily Suspending Alarming
Topic: Temporarily Suspending Alarming (Alarm Shelving or Alarm Inhibiting)
Question: What is Temporarily Suspending Alarming (Alarm Shelving or Alarm Inhibiting)?
Answer:
Temporarily suspending alarming, also known as alarm shelving or inhibiting, allows you to remove an alarm from the entire system for a specific time period. This is typically done during maintenance on a plant section or equipment, or when an alarm indicator is malfunctioning or being tested. You can suspend alarming globally per Alarm agent or individually per incident, specifying the time when the alarm will be re-enabled.

Answer:
Temporarily Suspending Alarming allows you to disable specific alarmed incidents for a defined future time. Title: The Accumulator Agent
Topic: Operation
Question: What is Operation?
Answer:
The Accumulator Agent operates by immediately starting a new period when intervalMode is set to 4. It then calculates a new value at the end of each period by subtracting the startValue from the inputValue, saving this lastValue. If a SQL Server connection is configured, the agent also adds a record to the history table with the period end time, value, and current inputValue.
Category: Smart UI - Agents
Document Type: help
Section Type: help

Title: The Accumulator Agent
Topic: Trigger event
Question: What is Trigger event?
Answer:
A trigger event causes the Accumulator Agent to subtract the previous interval input value from the current input value, calculating the value differential for the current period. This differential represents the total production for the last hour, shift, or day, and the agent then calculates the rate of change in value.

Title: The Accumulator Agent
Topic: Operation
Question: What is Operation?
Answer:
The Accumulator Agent begins a new period immediately when intervalMode is set to 4. Otherwise, it starts a period that ends at the next synchronized period. At the end of each period, the previous value is saved, and a new value is calculated by subtracting the starting value from the input value. A record is added to the history table with period end time, current inputValue, and the value for the period if a SQL Server connection is configured.

Title: The Agent Server Window Tray Icon

Title: The AgentGroup Agent
Question: What is The AgentGroup Agent?
Answer:
The AgentGroup Agent is a container used to combine related agents into groups. These groups can have overlapping memberships, and the AgentGroup Agent adapts its status based on its members – in normal mode, it simply holds the agents, while in fan in status bits mode, it mirrors the status of its members. You can configure which agent slots are exposed to the Adroit OPC Server using the 'exposeViaOpc' field.

Title: The Analog Agent
Question: What is The Analog Agent?
Answer:
The Analog Agent is a device that stores a real (floating-point) value and provides scaling functionality based on user-defined minimum and maximum settings. It supports up to 51-bit numbers, monitors its value against alarm limits, and calculates statistics every second. This agent also tracks value changes and their timestamps for logging and alarming.

Title: The Backup Directory Structure when Overwrite is disabled
Question: What is The Backup Directory Structure when Overwrite is Disabled?
Answer:
The backup path you specify is the root for folders containing individual backups, named by their creation date and time. Within each backup folder, you may find data, events, reg, and sys folders containing the Adroit data files, event logs, registry files, and installation files, respectively, all in a specified compressed format.

Title: The Backup Directory Structure when Overwrite is enabled
Question: What is The Backup Directory Structure when Overwrite is enabled?
Answer:
When overwrite is enabled, the backup directory structure includes the data folder (containing Adroit data files), the events folder (containing event logs), the reg folder (containing Adroit registry files), and the sys folder (containing Adroit installation files). Files within these folders will be overwritten if they match files being backed up.

Answer:
The Command Agent allows you to send and receive SMS messages up to 160 characters, bypassing scanning limitations. It can also receive commands within these messages to remotely monitor and control your process, such as acknowledging alarms or fetching process values. This agent is designed to work with a GSM_SMS modem and is configured to handle both sending and receiving SMS messages.

Question: What is Parameters on startup?
Answer:
The following parameters must be configured in Adroit Setup (Config) before the Agent Server is started: startMaxChannels (maximum number of channels), startGranularity (time granularity in seconds), startProject (current project name, limited to 8 characters without spaces), startName (unique server name, limited to 7 characters), startLoadFile (agent database file), maxAgents (total number of agents), startSaveOnExit (whether to save the WGP file on exit), and startDebug (debug flags for advanced users).

Question: What is The Counter Agent?
Answer:
takes data from any Input Tag’s BOOLEAN slot and calculates the time spent On (1) and the time spent Off (0), counts the number of On and Off events, and totalises the On and Off time. Title: The DBLog Agent
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
- DBLog1 writes data to Table1 and is configured with no housekeeping: So housekeeping will NOT run on Table1, as expected. - DBLog2 writes data to Table2 and housekeeping is configured: So the specified housekeeping WILL run on Table2, as expected. - DBLog3 and DBLog4 writes data to the same table Table34 - - DBLog3 is configured with no housekeeping AND - DBLog4 is configured with 30 days housekeeping: So Housekeeping WILL run on Table34 as per DBLog4’s housekeeping configuration for this SHARED table.

Title: The Device Agent
Question: What is The Device Agent?
Answer:
The Device Agent manages the communication settings of one or more tags for a device that has been added to a protocol driver. It connects to a front-end device, automatically creates Scan agents to manage tag scanning configurations (such as poll rate and timestamps), and can stop and start communication with the front-end device, configuring its settings as needed. These Scan agents are dynamically created and removed when tags are unscanned.

Title: The Effect of Combining Scanning Settings
Question: What is The Effect of Combining Scanning Settings?
Answer:
Combining scanning settings can impact the synchronization between a tag's process value and its Agent Server value. Specifically, changes to global scanning settings require restarting the Agent Server, while tag-specific settings require restarting the scanning device(s). Furthermore, if the scan inhibit bit is enabled, there are no guarantees the Agent Server value will match the process value.

Title: The Effect of Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers
Topic: Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers
Question: What is Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers?
Answer:
Shadowed cluster servers are designed to protect the system by preventing Classic UIs from connecting to standby servers that have not yet initialized. When a new standby server starts, any UIs configured to connect to it will display telemetry tags as "greyed-out" or "bad" because Adroit cannot immediately determine their health due to unsolicited telemetry data. To resolve this, you can restart the devices on the master server, swap the master and standby roles, or allow the standby to automatically become healthy when it takes over as master.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: shadowed cluster, telemetry, standby, cluster
Source URL: https://ats-adroit.github.io/mysoftware-help/chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/AU_01_04/The_Effect_of_Using_Shadowed_Cluster_Servers_with_Drivers.htm
Source File: chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/AU_01_04/The_Effect_of_Using_Shadowed_Cluster_Servers_with_Drivers.htm

---

Title: The Effect of Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers
Topic: Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers
Question: What is Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers?
Answer:
Shadowed cluster servers, when a second cluster partner is started in standby mode, can cause Classic UIs to display "greyed-out" or marked-bad tags linked to "telemetry" device(s). This is because Adroit doesn't know which tags are healthy at startup due to the unsolicited nature of telemetry. To resolve this, stop and restart the affected devices on the master server, swap master and standby, or leave it alone if the standby takes over as master and automatically becomes healthy.

Title: The EventLogging Agent
Question: What is The EventLogging Agent?
Answer:
The EventLogging Agent logs events from Adroit to either the Applications event log on any Windows computer or to an OLE DB compatible database like MS Access or MS SQL. These events include undesirable states, process values, and control device malfunctions, and are used to analyze process conditions over time. The agent can log various event types like alarm acknowledgements, change monitoring, control actions, system events, and jottings.

Title: The ICMP Agent
Topic: The ICMP or PING Agent
Question: What is The ICMP or PING Agent?
Answer:
The ICMP Agent uses the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) to check if remote devices are reachable on your network. It works by continuously sending and receiving ICMP messages, typically through the PING utility, and generating alarms if errors occur or the round trip time exceeds defined limits.

Title: The IOT Agent
Topic: Example of the XML structure
Question: What is Example of the XML structure?
Answer:
The XML structure for the IOT Agent uses the `<IOT>` tag, containing `<Slots>` and `<HeaderSlots>`. An example XML structure is `<IOT Name="Fridge1" Description="Fridge in kitchen"><Slots><Slot Name="value" Description="Temperature" Type="Real">20</Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots><Slot Name="hi"/> </HeaderSlots></IOT> or <IOT><SlotDefinitions><Slot Name="value" Description="Temperature" Type="Real">20</Slot></SlotDefinitions><HeaderSlots><Slot Name="hi"/> </HeaderSlots></IOT>.

Title: The Marshal Agent
Question: What is The Marshal Agent?
Answer:
The Marshal Agent replaces the Marshalling function of the Multistate agent by gathering binary data from its 16-bit rawvalue or value slot. It allows individual bits to be alarmed, pulsed, named, and reflects the ON or OFF state of each bit, extending the alarming subsystem.

Title: The Marshal Agent
Question: What is The Marshal Agent?
Answer:
is designed to replace the popular marshalling function of the Multistate agent, by gathering discreet binary data from its 16 bit rawvalue or value slot. By giving each of the individual bits the full functionality of a digital agent, exceeds the former capabilities of a marshalled mode Multistate Agent. These bits can then be alarmed, pulsed, named, and the 1 and 0 states of each bit can be named (on/off, open/closed etc).

Title: The Notify Agent
Question: What is The Notify Agent?
Answer:
The Notify Agent provides an alarm route destination that sends alarms via SMS or paging services to keep off-site personnel informed of unacknowledged alarms, process values, and operator messages. It supports various paging services like Zetron encoder, MTN, Vodacom, Autopage, and Telstra, and can also send email messages to designated recipients. When configuring, ensure scan rates are set to zero for Notify agent slots displayed on mimics to prevent errors.

Title: The PerfMon Agent

Answer:
is used to monitor Windows Performance counters, which belong to performance objects such as the Agent Server, Processor, Memory, and others. These counters facilitate the monitoring of the computers performance and assist in detecting performance bottlenecks that could adversely affect the functioning of Adroit . Title: The PID Agent
Question: What is The PID Agent?
Answer:
The PID Agent is a faceplate agent designed for external PID controllers. It encapsulates the 25 signals and tuning parameters associated with a PID, allowing these values to be transmitted via raw slots to reduce the number of agents needed in a project. Configurable high and low operation limits are provided for the SP and CV slots to prevent potentially harmful values from being set.

Title: The Primitive Agents
Question: What is The Primitive Agents?
Answer:
The Primitive Agents (Boolean, Integer, Real, and String) are the simplest agent types used to hold single values. These agents are suitable for scenarios where memory efficiency is a priority, but they do not support advanced features like alarming or SCADA functionality. The String agent now includes a 'valueex' slot to handle strings longer than 79 characters, though this slot is not supported by the scanning subsystem.

Title: The Primitive Agents
Question: What is The Primitive Agents?
Answer:
The Primitive Agents (Boolean, Integer, Real, and String) are the simplest agent types used to hold a single value. They lack features like inversion or linearisation found in more complex agent types and are primarily used when efficient memory use is a priority. The String agent has been updated to support longer strings (up to 79 characters) via a new 'valueex' slot, which is not supported by the scanning subsystem.

Title: The Shift Agent
Question: What is The Shift Agent?
Answer:
Steps: Various agents in Adroit , such as OEE, require knowing the current shift number. Instead of configuring the shift pattern information into each instance of these agents, you can instead configure these shift patterns globally, in a Shift agent, for use by any interested agents. The value slot of should also be scanned, output enabled, to any PLCs that perform any shift end functions, such as resetting shift count accumulators.

Title: Time Stamping
Question: What is Time Stamping?
Answer:
Time stamping in Adroit is created when a value is scanned or entered manually. The timestamp originates from the system clock and propagates through agents, subscriptions, and the user interface, including mimics and picture elements. Tampering with the system clock can cause significant disruptions to mimic updates, datalogging, and existing alarms.

Time stamping in Adroit is achieved by recording the creation time of data. Data packets from front-end devices and manual user inputs are timestamped using the system clock, and this timestamp is then propagated through agents and into the user interface, mimicking, and picture elements.

Title: Time Synchronization of an Adroit Cluster
Topic: Time Synchronization
Question: What is Time Synchronization?
Answer:
Time synchronization is critical for Adroit cluster operation, ensuring all Agent Servers and clients share a common time source. Unsynchronized system times can lead to issues like UI updates failing, trend data displaying incorrect behavior, and data logs becoming corrupted. This typically involves using the Windows Time service.

Title: Timer Agent - Slot Details
Topic: Slots:
Question: What is Slots?:
Answer:
Slots are configurable parameters that control the Timer Agent's behavior. The `autoReset` slot automatically resets the timer after a specified duration, while the `delayTime` slot sets the delay before a pulse is triggered. The `freeRun` slot enables pulse generator mode, and the `granularity` slot determines how frequently the timer monitors time.

Title: Title 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance
Question: What is Title 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance?
Answer:
Title 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance is the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) guideline on electronic records and electronic signatures (ERES). This regulation defines criteria for electronic records and signatures to be considered trustworthy and reliable, equivalent to paper records, ensuring they meet FDA standards.

Title: To Configure Automatic Logon

Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
To configure automatic logon on Windows, navigate to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE extbackslash Software extbackslash Microsoft extbackslash WindowsNT extbackslash CurrentVersion extbackslash WinLogon. Set the 'AutoAdminLogon' value to '1', the 'DefaultPassword' value to your desired password, and the 'DefaultUserName' and 'DefaultDomainName' values to reflect the user account you want to use.

Title: To Configure the SystemDatalog Agent for Datalog Catchup
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
Datalog catch-up only applies to clustered Agent Servers and refers to the process of synchronizing, unsynchronised sections of logged data between the two Agent Server partners in the cluster. This involves fetching stored historical data from the datalog agents on the cluster partner and merging the data with the local datalog agents. Note: For performance reasons, the SystemDatalog agent ONLY provides the Time datalog catchup method, of catching up the data between two specified date/times.

Title: To Configure the Update Rate of Data from the OPC Server
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
The OPC Server update rate, specified in milliseconds, determines how frequently the server provides data to connected clients. The default rate is 250 ms, which is the fastest available. To change this value, click on the Edit menu and select Properties to open the Adroit OPC Server Configuration dialog, and specify the rate in the Server update rate (ms) edit box.

Title: To Create a Half Hour Average of a Process Input
Question: What is To Create a Half Hour Average of a Process Input?
Answer:
To create a half-hourly average of process input like TEMP1, you need to set up a pulse that triggers every 100 ms, an expression to filter the pulse based on minute intervals, and a reset pulse. Then, use a statistical agent to average the input and configure it to transfer the data to a database triggered by the reset pulse.

Question: What is To Create a Half Hour Average of a Process Input?

Question: What is Disabling the Task Manager for the Current User?

This change will immediately disable the Task Manager for that user.

Title: To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging
Question: What is To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging?
Answer:
To estimate the disk space required for data logging, calculate the maximum space each agent may occupy based on the logging period, logging rate, and the number of tags being logged. This calculation considers the size of the raw data log file (.LGD) and its index file (.LGI), as well as the potential for log backups (.LDB) to extend the data logging period. Adroit reserves 20% of the calculated space, unless a clean installation is performed, in which case the proprietary logging factor is not applied.
Category: Smart UI - Logging

Section Type: help

Title: To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging
Question: What is To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging?
Answer:
To estimate the disk space needed for data logging, consider the actual buffer size and file size based on the logging period and rate. The buffer size calculation uses a factor of 20, but this is only suitable for fast logging rates (e.g., 1 second). Slower rates (e.g., 1 minute or 1 hour) require over-specifying the logging period by a factor of 5, as the agent will only have capacity to log for 1/5th of the configured period. You can adjust this by setting the LogCompressionFactor registry setting.
Category: Smart UI - Logging
Document Type: help

Title: To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging
Question: What is To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging?
Answer:
The user has no direct control over the speed at which the raw data log file will grow. Therefore, it is important to calculate the maximum space each agent may occupy, before the data log file wraps around and overwrites itself from the beginning. This figure can be compared to the actual free disk space available on the host computer.

Title: To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging
Question: What is To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging?
Answer:
To estimate the disk space required for data logging, calculate the actual buffer size based on the logging period and logging rate. The buffer size is then summed to determine the file size. You should consider that slower logging rates may necessitate over-specifying the logging period by a factor of 5, and the datalog agent can handle up to 53 million records, potentially logging for 30 days at a rate of 50 milliseconds. You can also create multiple log files for agents with different logging speeds.

Question: How do I configure Toshiba T2 Ethernet in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The Toshiba T2 Ethernet device uses a message protocol with a checksum calculated from the ASCII code of the lower two digits of the sum of all values of bytes in the message, starting from the first byte until the "&" termination byte. Title: Transaction Types of DbAccess Agents
Question: What is Transaction Types of DbAccess Agents?
Answer:
The DbAccess agent supports four transaction types: Insert, Update, Delete, and Retrieve. The Insert transaction adds new records to a table, while the Update transaction modifies existing records. The Delete transaction removes rows, and the Retrieve transaction fetches data from a row.

Title: Type List CSV File Format
Question: What is Type List CSV File Format?
Answer:
This file, named xxxxx-TYPLST.CSV, is created when an Alarm agent is exported to store its alarm types. The file contains columns for Alarm type, Agent type, Bit-mask (calculated as 2^n), and Value, and the rows are sorted alphabetically using the alarm type name as an index.

Title: Type List CSV File Format
Question: What is Type List CSV File Format?
Answer:
The Type List CSV file stores alarm types created for an Alarm agent. It's named xxxxx-TYPLST.CSV and contains columns for alarm type, agent type, bit-mask, and value, sorted alphabetically by alarm type name. The bit-mask represents the sum of bit positions (2^n) from 16 through 31, indicating alarm off-states (0 normal, 1 off).

Answer:
To implement a UDT agent type, you must first stop your Agent Server, then launch the UDT Agent Type Designer and configure its properties (component data types) and status slots. After this, you must start the Agent Server and create instances of the UDT agent type, scanning them into the corresponding PLCs. You must also remove all existing agent instances from the Adroit agent database (.WGP) file when changing the UDT agent structure.

Title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features
Topic: Optimised scan tasks
Question: What is Optimised scan tasks?
Answer:
Optimised scan tasks, as implemented by NASA, combine different Agent types (such as Analog, Digital, etc.) and data type formats (longs, words, dwords) within a single scan job. This minimizes the number of separate transactions, leading to improved throughput and reduced communication overhead when scanning process values to and from Adroit.

Title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features
Topic: Improved multi-channel performance
Question: What is Improved multi-channel performance?
Answer:
Previously, only specific legacy supported multi channels, such as Modbus EMC or Modbus Radio. All NASA provide support for multi channels although this feature is off by default. When enabled, NASA can support up to 8 channels, which are utilised as-needed to service the required transactions to achieve parallel communication on a single device.

Title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features
Topic: Demand Scanning
Question: What is Demand Scanning?
Answer:
Demand Scanning, supported by the NASA driver, is a protocol designed to optimize communication by only transmitting process values when they are actively being used. Specifically, it's used for read-only values displayed on graphics or utilized by graphic form components like behaviours. This reduces data transfer costs and improves network throughput, especially over telemetry or satellite communications.

Title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features
Topic: Usage scenarios NOT recommended for demand scanning:
Question: What is Usage scenarios NOT recommended for demand scanning?
Answer:
Demand scanning is not recommended for process values that are being alarmed, actively logged, or used by another Adroit agent. Specifically, using demand scanning with 'Output Enabled' is constantly scanning and cannot be demand scanned. Furthermore, it’s not recommended for clustered Agent Servers with shadow scanning and a proxy server, as this can return incorrect values.

Title: Usage Guidelines for DbAccess Agents
Question: What is Usage Guidelines for DbAccess Agents?
Answer:
DbAccess Agents are designed to transfer multiple tags in a single transaction from OLE DB Servers to databases, making them more efficient than traditional datalog agents for periodic data reporting. These agents retrieve data from OLE DB Servers and are best suited for applications where data is written to a database at intervals, such as at the end of a batch job. Careful consideration should be given to the number of agents and the amount of work they perform to avoid excessive resource usage.

Title: Using Analog Agent Alarm Limits
Topic: Limitations
Question: What is Limitations?
Answer:
The Low (lo slot), High (hi slot), Low-low (loLo slot), and High-high (hiHi slot) inner and outer alarm limits are warning indicators that a process value has moved outside its acceptable range. If the Low or High limits are triggered, the corresponding outer alarm will also activate, indicating urgent corrective action is needed.

Title: Using Analog Agent Alarm Limits
Topic: Limitations
Question: What is Limitations?
Answer:
The Rate of Change limit defines the maximum change in an engineering value within one second. If the value changes more than this limit, the Rate of Change status bit is set. This limit is independent of the low-low, low, high, and high-high limits.

Title: Value formatting syntax
Question: What is Value formatting syntax?
Answer:
Value formatting syntax uses a string format defined by the following syntax: `{ # [, alignment ][: dataFormat ]}`. The '#' denotes a unique input number, typically starting from 0, and the alignment component is a signed integer specifying the preferred field width. The dataFormat component allows customization of the display of values using format specifiers like numeric formats (e.g., {0:X} for hexadecimal).
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: value formatting, syntax, format string, alignment, dataFormat

Title: Visual property indicators
Topic: Spider property indicators
Question: What is Spider property indicators?
Answer:
Spider property indicators appear in the spider title bar to show when associated properties are enabled. A colon (:) indicates the Trigger Spider on Event property is enabled, while a double colon (:) indicates the Propagate Outputs At Startup property is enabled. These indicators disappear when the properties are disabled.

Title: Visual property indicators
Topic: Silk property indicators
Question: What is Silk property indicators?
Answer:
Silk property indicators use symbols to show the status of the Trigger Output Spider property for each silk. A hyphen (-) indicates the property is disabled, meaning the spider will not trigger when the value changes. A plus sign (+) indicates the property is enabled, and the spider will trigger when the value changes.

Title: VIZNETDataBinder components
Question: What is VIZNETDataBinder components?

The VIZNETDataBinder component is a hidden form component that allows for bi-directional communication with an OLE DB datasource. It enables you to create a subset of data from the datasource, allowing you to view and modify the data in real-time. This component utilizes BindingSource and DataSet components to manage data access and retrieval.

Title: VIZNETDataBinder components
Question: What is VIZNETDataBinder components?
Answer:
VIZNETDataBinder components are recommended for viewing large datasets in a spreadsheet environment. They include a toolbar (VIZNETBindingNavigator control) that allows users to view, navigate, and modify data by communicating with the associated BindingSource component. If you do not use the Create Controls option, you must implement your own method of communicating to the BindingSource components, such as using the DataBinderTrigger spider.

Title: VIZNETDataBinder components task menu
Topic: Triggering
Question: What is Triggering?
Answer:
Triggering automatically loads data for associated VIZNETBindingNavigator controls when the graphic form is opened. This behavior is enabled by setting the AutoLoad property to True, and you can select which tables to automatically load using the AutoLoad List property. The Trigger Control setting specifies which control initiates this auto-loading process.

Title: VIZNETDataBinder components task menu
Topic: Settings
Question: What is Settings?
Answer:
- BindingNavigator List: The list of VIZNETBindingNavigator controls that are auto loaded by this component. This allows you to manually add VIZNETBindingNavigator controls for this VIZNETDataBinder component. - BindingSource List: The list of VIZNETBindingSource components that are updated by this component. This allows you to manually add VIZNETBindingSource components for this VIZNETDataBinder component. - ParameterSource List: The list of parameters used by the selected DataBinder, which can be used to link controls to provide the values of these parameters.

Title: What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it?
Question: What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it??
Answer:
Maximum demand is an additional cost applied by your electricity provider to control your usage during peak times, specifically when your power usage aligns with peak domestic usage. It’s defined as the maximum amount of electricity you're allowed to use during these periods, measured in kVAh, and your provider monitors your usage in 30-minute block periods. Monitoring maximum demand is crucial to avoid costly penalties and can lead to significant savings through power management.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: maximum demand, peak demand, power monitoring, electricity cost

Title: What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it?
Question: What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it??
Answer:
Maximum demand is an additional cost charged by your electricity provider to control your energy usage during peak times, specifically when your usage aligns with peak domestic demand. It's defined as the maximum amount of electricity you're allowed to use during those periods, measured in kVAh, and your provider monitors your usage in 30-minute blocks. Monitoring maximum demand can result in considerable savings and reduced power usage, but it's recommended to automate this monitoring.

Title: Working with 21 CFR 11 mode
Topic: What 21 CFR 11 mode enforces (design-restrictions):
Question: What is What 21 CFR 11 mode enforces (design-restrictions):?
Answer:
21 CFR 11 compliance requires limiting system access to authorised individuals. Therefore the connection to the Adroit Agent Server is now secured to limit exactly which client connection to it is allowed to prevent unsanctioned access (from Classic or legacy Adroit Clients and third party applications). Note: This means that one cannot use the Configurator to configure Adroit agents in the SmartUI Designer when using 21 CFR 11 mode - so all Agent Server configuration must occur in the Designer itself.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: spec
Keywords: 11, with, working with 21 cfr 11 mode, adroit scada, adroit, cfr, html, smart ui - other, working, mode, 21

Title: Working with 21 CFR 11 mode
Topic: Requirements
Question: What is Requirements?
Answer:
To enable 21 CFR 11 mode, you must create Windows users and groups and configure them as 'allowed' on each SmartUI Server. Only system administrators should have extended rights, and their users/groups must be specified in the Security Settings page of the Adroit Config Editor to prevent unauthorized access and potential disruption of the audit mechanism.

Title: Working with audited data element values
Question: What is Working with audited data element values?
Answer:
Audited data element values are stored in two databases: a mandatory, local SQL Server Compact database on the SmartUI Server and an optional user-defined SQL Server database. The local database is designed to prevent connection loss and is always backed up with the Configuration. The optional database is configured through the Adroit Config Editor utility by selecting ‘Yes’ for the Auditing question in the Server Security Settings page and specifying the connection string.
Category: Smart UI - Security
Document Type: help

Keywords: auditing, data elements, databases, SmartUI Server

Title: Working with Categories
Question: What is Working with Categories?
Answer:
Categories in the Edit AlarmManagement Agent dialog allow you to define areas of your process controlled by operators and create a logical framework for querying incidents. This involves arranging categories hierarchically, using examples such as Country, City, Site, Process area, Unit name, PID number, and Instrument tag number, to organize incidents effectively. You can add, rename, and move categories, but only to the default Root category. Configuring the 'Operator tag' setting for categories helps ensure incidents are logged with the correct operator’s name.

Title: Working with Configurations
Topic: Configuration
Question: What is Configuration?
Answer:
Configurations in Adroit and SmartUI are independent sets of files, application settings, and registry keys, allowing for the separation of systems. These configurations are managed via the Configuration page, where you can select one active configuration at a time to control the functionality of Adroit and SmartUI applications. Only one configuration can be loaded and used, and changes to this configuration require a restart of all applications.

Title: Working with SmartUI Templates
Question: What is Working with SmartUI Templates?
Answer:
SmartUI Templates are reusable graphic forms that can be used at run-time. The fundamental difference between a graphic form and a SmartUI Template is that a SmartUI Template has aliases, some of which are automatically created, which allow data elements within Behaviours and/or spiders to be dynamically driven. Typically SmartUI Templates are used for graphic forms that are displayed as pop-ups or within TemplateGO a Template Graphic Object control that displays a graphic form and connects data elements to any aliases of this graphic form.

Question: What is Important differences between a HASP and a soft license?
Answer:

Title: Working with the Adtech Licensing Utility
Topic: How to get a new HASP license or update an existing one:
Question: What is How to get a new HASP license or update an existing one:?
Answer:
Steps: If necessary, launch the Adtech Licensing Utility first. PLEASE NOTE: Purple HASPs are not supported (they lack the necessary space required by this licensing mechanism). - Ensure that your HASP is inserted into the computer. If necessary, click the Rescan HASPs button in the lower right corner. The Request HASP Update button should now be enabled. If the Request HASP Update button is disabled then there is a problem reading your HASP, in which case do the following: - Click the Status tab and right click this page and click the Select all menu item.

Title: Working with the Adtech Licensing Utility
Topic: Important licensing changes:
Question: What is Important licensing changes?:
Answer:
The product license is now an XML document for easier reading, and the old Remote Nodes licenses are no longer supported. Instead, clients (Operators and Designers) and Web Clients (Performance Anywhere) now use client-specific node licenses with different costs. Remote Desktop (RDP) clients can get free connections to the Agent Server by configuring the RDAdminName WG.INI registry string.

Title: Working with the Adtech Licensing Utility
Topic: Important differences between a HASP and a soft license:
Question: What is Important differences between a HASP and a soft license?
Answer:
HASP licenses are tied to a USB HASP device with a unique serial number, making them portable but carrying security risks and requiring self-insurance. In contrast, soft licenses are bound to a specific computer and cannot be transferred; if that computer fails, the license becomes invalid.

Title: Working with the Health Monitor Service
Topic: What does it do?
Question: What does the Health Monitor Service do?
Answer:
The Health Monitor Service periodically checks computer information and process usage to identify potential performance issues. Specifically, it monitors CPU usage, memory, and drive space, as well as specific processes like as.exe, VIP Designer.exe, and VIP Server.exe. It flags processes based on CPU and memory usage thresholds and logs events when processes exceed these limits.

Title: Working with the Health Monitor Service
Topic: How to add additional processes to be monitored
Question: What is How to add additional processes to be monitored?
Answer:
Steps: If necessary, you can add additional Processes to be monitored by the Health Monitor Service. The configuration file resides in installation folder of the Health Monitor Service (typically found - C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Common\Health Monitor). The configuration file is called HealthMonitorConfig.xml Example Configuration Entry to add the Notepad.exe process to the list of monitored processes, add the following to the end of this file, above the </NewDataSet> line: <Executables> <Executable>Notepad.exe</Executable> <CPUCoreThresholdPercent>2</CPUCoreThresholdPercent> <PrivateBytesLimit>1146880000</PrivateBytesLimit> <PrivateBytesThresholdPercent>80</PrivateBytesThresholdPercent> </Executables>
Category: Smart UI - Configuration
Document Type: configuration
Section Type: procedural

You can add additional Processes to be monitored by the Health Monitor Service by modifying the HealthMonitorConfig.xml file located in the Health Monitor Service's installation folder (typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Common\Health Monitor). To add a process, such as Notepad.exe, add the following within the </NewDataSet> tag: `<Executables> <Executable>Notepad.exe</Executable> <CPUCoreThresholdPercent>2</CPUCoreThresholdPercent> <PrivateBytesLimit>1146880000</PrivateBytesLimit> <PrivateBytesThresholdPercent>80</PrivateBytesThresholdPercent> </Executables>`.

Title: Working with the object model
Topic: How does the object model work?
Question: What is How does the object model work??
Answer:
The object model allows you to create and reuse pre-configured SCADA objects, such as pumps and motors, by defining both their graphical representation and the associated SCADA configuration. You create a template from a wizard, specifying the graphical representation and SCADA settings, and then create instances of the template, which automatically configures agents and provides the graphical representation. This approach promotes mass reuse and standardization of SCADA configurations for similar objects.

Title: Working with the SimCSV driver
Topic: CSV File Structure
Question: What is CSV File Structure?
Answer:
The SimCSV driver CSV file structure defines how data is written to addresses. Specifically, it includes: Seq T+x (specifies the delay before address changes), Address (the address to write to), and Value (the value to write). The first three entries are required, and others can be omitted; however, if time offsets are configured, the order of value changes isn't determined by the CSV row order.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help

Title: Working with the SimCSV driver
Topic: Optional Parameters
Question: What is Optional Parameters?
Answer:
Optional parameters in the SimCSV driver allow you to specify a time offset from the sequence's current time, either forward or backward in time. You can also define a fixed timestamp using an IEEE754 float string or an OLEDT, taking into account the system locale settings. Importantly, you cannot update an item to a historical time and mark it bad at the same time; you can only mark the latest value bad at the current time.

Answer:
The SimCSV driver uses a CSV file to define a sequence of timed events. Title: Write Only Scanning Strategy
Topic: Operation of strategy:
Question: What is Operation of strategy?
Answer:
The Agent Server receives scanned tag values from front-end devices (PLCs) when the system is started. However, if SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan is set to 1, the Agent Server does not initially receive these values. Unhealthy states occur when a device stops or starts, or after communication failures are resolved.

Title: WriteThreadStacksize
Question: What is WriteThreadStacksize?
Answer:
WriteThreadStacksize is a registry key that controls the amount of space available for tag write-threads when output is enabled. To modify this setting, add the following registry key and value: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\[Wow6432Node]\]SOFTWARE\[Adroit Technologies]\[Adroit]\[Scanning. The default value is 256 KB, but you can adjust it to the required amount in kilobytes.
Category: Smart UI - Alarming
Document Type: help
Section Type: configuration
Keywords: WriteThreadStacksize, registry, tag write-threads, output
Source URL: https://ats-adroit.github.io/mysoftware-help/chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/AU_01_02/WriteThreadStacksize.htm
Source File: chm_extracted/Smart_UI/Designer/AU_01_02/WriteThreadStacksize.htm

---

Title: WriteThreadStacksize
Question: What is WriteThreadStacksize?
Answer:
The WriteThreadStacksize registry setting controls the amount of space available for tag write-threads, specifically affecting output enabled tag writes to front-end devices. You can modify this value in the registry by adding the key HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Scanning and setting the DWORD value to the required amount in kilobytes (the default is 256 KB). However, this setting should only be changed with guidance from the Support Desk.

Title: Writing Scheduled Entries to the Registry
Question: What is Writing Scheduled Entries to the Registry?
Answer:
Writing scheduled entries to the registry ensures that changes to the scheduler's entries are saved, eliminating the need for the scheduler to remain running to schedule new or modified entries. This process is triggered when you terminate the Scheduler application, which you can do by right-clicking the icon in the tray bar or by selecting the 'Terminate' button within the Scheduler window.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: scheduled entries, registry, scheduler

Title: Writing Scheduled Entries to the Registry
Question: What is Writing Scheduled Entries to the Registry?
Answer:
After modifying scheduled entries, you must write the changes to the registry to ensure the Scheduler doesn't need to remain running to schedule entries. This is done by terminating the Scheduler application through the tray icon or the Scheduler window.

Title: Writing scripts
Question: What is Writing scripts?
Answer:
Scripts are created within the script editor specified by the user's profile, defaulting to either Microsoft Visual Basic .NET or Microsoft C# (CSharp). These scripts interact with the SmartUI Server and Client through INeed interfaces and can include references to external assemblies (.DLL files) to extend functionality. The script includes an Initialise function that contains pre-execution configuration and variable definitions, and a Main function which is the only entry point for the script.
